Document Title: Decree No. 06/2022/ND-CP on Mitigation of Green House Gas (GHG) Emissions and Protection of Ozone Layer

Family Name: Marine Ecological Environment Protection Plan for the 14th Five-Year Period
Family Summary: This Plan sets out the adaptation actions to strengthen the ability of the marine environment to adapt to climate change impacts alongside the reduction of marine pollution. The Plan also states that feasibility studies will be carried out on blue carbon sinks.
Document Title: Marine Ecological Environment Protection Plan for the 14th Five-Year Period

Family Name: Finland's National Forest Strategy 2035
Family Summary: Finland’s National Forest Strategy 2035 is the statutory national forest programme guiding Finland’s forest policy towards 2035. It coordinates economic, environmental and social objectives and responds to changes in the forest sector, including climate change and biodiversity loss. Its vision is to create growing wellbeing from forests and for forests, with priorities focused on increasing forest growth, carbon sequestration and timber production, strengthening biodiversity in commercial forests, and creating a competitive and responsible forest-based sector. The strategy also emphasises sustainable and diverse forest use, forest resilience, and knowledge-based management.
Document Title: Finland's National Forest Strategy 2035

Family Name: Plan of Action for Cocoa and Forests Initiative (ICF) 2022-2025
Family Summary:
The Cocoa and Forests Initiative (ICF) is a joint partnership of the governments of Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana, and 35 companies in the cocoa and chocolate sector representing 85% of the world's cocoa trade, aimed at eliminating deforestation from the cocoa supply chain and combating climate change. Actions also include practising climate-smart agroforestry.

The first phase of the ICF implementation, from 2018 to 2020, which served as a pilot phase, focused on the implementation of projects carried out individually or in small coalitions by the signatories of the initiative.

This Phase II for 2022-2025 will remain focused on the three (3) pillars of the ICF, namely:

1. Forest protection and restoration: the implementation of large-scale public-private partnership projects for the protection and restoration of classified forests and selected parks and reserves, and surrounding landscapes. The classified forests of Yapo-Abbé (24,592 ha), Tamin (24,934 ha), and Cavally (64,200 ha), the Mont-Péko National Park (34,000 ha), the Mabi-Yaya Reserve (61,282 ha), and the Bossématié Reserve (21,550 ha), along with their surrounding areas, are among the priority landscapes identified for these public-private partnerships.

2. Agroforestry and sustainable cocoa production: These themes are promoted through sustainability programs implemented by the ICF signatories. Strengthening the mapping of cocoa supply chains, with the establishment of a national traceability system, is a key priority for the signatories under this pillar.

3. Community Participation and Social Inclusion: Strengthening activities for greater social inclusion and community engagement. It should be noted that community participation will be taken into account in the implementation of all activities planned in the 2022-2025 action plan. The same applies to the gender aspect.
Document Title: Plan of Action for Cocoa and Forests Initiative (ICF) 2022-2025

Family Name: Agricultural Climate Solutions - Living Labs Program
Family Summary:
The goal of the Agricultural Climate Solutions Program (ACS) – Living Labs Program is to accelerate co-development, testing, adoption, dissemination and monitoring of technologies and practices, including beneficial management practices (BMPs), that sequester carbon and/or mitigate greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions.

Through a collaborative approach, projects will focus on the on-farm co-development, testing, adoption and monitoring of new BMPs and technologies. Projects funded under ACS will follow the living lab innovation approach. A living lab is an integrated approach to agricultural innovation that brings together farmers, scientists, and other participants to co-develop, test, and monitor new BMPs and technologies in a real-life context where they will be used: on Canadian farms.

The program will consider projects within the following 2 priority areas:

  • Carbon sequestration (for example, cover crops, intercropping, conversion of marginal land to permanent cover, shelterbelts, inclusion of pulses in rotations)
  • Greenhouse gas mitigation (for example, nutrient management, feeding strategies).

It is expected that approved comprehensive projects will start project activities in spring 2023.
Document Title: Agricultural Climate Solutions - Living Labs Program

Family Name: Guide for preparing the Regional Environmental Impact Statement
Family Summary: Mexico's Secretariat of Environment and Natural Resources (SEMARNAT) published the Technical Guidelines in 2022, which set out the requirements for preparing a Regional Environmental Impact Statement under the country's environmental assessment procedure. The guide establishes a framework requiring project proponents to identify cumulative environmental impacts. Proponents should identify greenhouse gas emissions and assess ecosystem vulnerability to climate change factors such as sea level rise, hurricanes, floods, and temperature increases, and use simulation models to project environmental factor changes over 5, 10, 15, and 20-year timeframes. Projects should include specific climate change adaptation and mitigation measures and disaster prevention and vulnerability reduction strategies.
Document Title: Technical Guidelines

Family Name: National Agroforestry Strategy 2022-2032
Family Summary: The strategy focuses on: the establishment of a policy and institutional basis for the wider promotion and adoption of agroforestry in The Gambia; the enhancement of coordination in agroforestry programmatic designs and implementation to promote institutional collaboration and technical backstopping; promotion of agroforestry knowledge creation, dissemination, adoption and monitoring for effective adoption of context-appropriate agroforestry practices at scale; adoption of investment mechanisms for agroforestry through wood and non-wood-based value chains promotion, including: multilateral environmental agreement, participatory forest management, protected areas, energy production through fuelwood; creation of an environment for inclusive participation of all stakeholders in agroforestry promotion and the associated value chains.
Document Title: National Agroforestry Strategy 2022-2032

Family Name: Taxonomy of Green Projects
Family Summary:
The “Classification (taxonomy) of “green” projects subject to financing through “green” bonds and “green” loans” (as approved by Decree of the Government of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 996 dated December 31, 2021) is a unified system of classification of economic activities, project categories, and assets aimed at increasing the efficiency of use of existing natural resources, lowering the level of negative environmental impacts, increasing energy efficiency, energy savings, climate change mitigation, and climate change adaptation.

According to the AIFC's (Astana International Finance Centre) Green Finance Centre (https://aifc.kz/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/green-finance-market-kz-10-m-2023.pdf), adoption of this Taxonomy contributed to market players’ rising interest in sustainable financial instruments as well as in projects on the transition of the country’s economy to low-carbon development.

This Taxonomy (updated on 27 March 2024) covers eight project categories:

  1. Renewable energy;
  2. Energy efficiency;
  3. Green buildings;
  4. Pollution prevention and control;
  5. Sustainable water use and waste;
  6. Sustainable agriculture, land management, forestry, biodiversity conservation and ecotourism;
  7. Clean transport; and
  8. Transitory energy (additional category).
Document Title: Taxonomy of Green Projects

Family Name: Decree of the President of Ukraine No. 111/2021
Family Summary: Promotion of actions to overcome the challenges and threats to the national security of Ukraine in the environment and define measures to neutralize them.Amongst the actions, the regulation focuses on environmental safety, in the development of a forest management strategy until 2035, and to combat and adapt to climate change by devoloping a national energy and climate change plan, a national energy efficiency action plan and a national plan for the development of renewable energy for the period up to 2030.
Document Title: Decree of the President of Ukraine No. 111/2021

Family Name: National Climate Finance Strategy of Belize 2021-2026
Family Summary: The National Climate Finance Strategy of Belize 2021-2026 notes that the ambition level of the country's NDCs is highly dependent on access to adequate finance, and as such the strategy aims to enhance climate financing for adaptation and mitigation in the short to medium term. As core strategic directions it aims to prioritise climate adaptation, leverage international private and public finance, promote domestic private climate finance, enhance financing based on carbon assets, climate-proof development projects across the economy, build a co-ordinated risk financing mechanism, and explore non-conventional climate finance strategies.
Document Title: National Climate Finance Strategy of Belize 2021-2026

Family Name: National Forest Strategy
Family Summary: The National Forest Strategy (SFN), adopted pursuant to Article 6(1) of Decreto Legislativo 3 aprile 2018, n. 34, establishes Italy’s strategic framework for the conservation, enhancement and sustainable management of the national forest heritage. Its overall aim is to protect and strengthen Italy’s forests so that they remain resilient, biodiversity-rich ecosystems capable of contributing to climate change mitigation and adaptation, while providing environmental, social and economic benefits. The strategy defines national guidelines for the development of the forestry sector and its related supply chains, in line with international and European commitments, including the EU Forest Strategy.The strategy is structured around three main objectives: (A) promoting sustainable forest management and the multifunctional role of forests, including biodiversity conservation, ecosystem services, land protection and climate mitigation; (B) improving the efficient use of forest resources to support sustainable economic development and strengthen forestry supply chains in rural, inland and urban areas; and (C) enhancing knowledge, research public awareness and international cooperation on forest policies.
Document Title: Interministerial Decree approving the National Forest Strategy

Family Name: The overall plan for the pilot program of the comprehensive reform of the market-based allocation of production factors (notice 51 of the State Office)
Family Summary:
This plan defines the government's plan for the pilot program on a wide range of reforms of the market determinants of production factors. It notably establishes 1) a system of green accounting, 2) the concept of ecological products value realisation, and 3) environmental responsibility for public and private entities. 

Section 24 of the document states that the government will support the creation of a "green factor trading mechanism". This would notably entail the trading of carbon emission rights, pollution discharge rights, energy use rights, water rights, etc. The government will also also explore other schemes, such as a paid-for-acquisition mechanism for carbon emission quotas and energy use rights indicators.
Document Title: The overall plan for the pilot program of the comprehensive reform of the market-based allocation of production factors (notice 51 of the State Office)

Family Name: Administrative Measures for Legal (ESG) Disclosure of Enterprise Environmental Information
Family Summary:
These measures aim to standardise  legal disclosure of corporate environmental information (ESG) "and strengthen social supervision, in accordance with the Environmental Protection Law, the Cleaner Production Promotion Law, the Measures for the Formulation of Provisions on Information Disclosure by Public Enterprises and Institutions, and the Legal Disclosure of Environmental Information. These Measures are applicable to the disclosure of environmental information by enterprises in accordance with the law and their supervision and management activities (art. 2). The Ministry of Ecology and Environment shall be responsible for the organisation, guidance, supervision and management of the legal disclosure of environmental information across the country (art. 3).

Under Chapter III on disclosure content and time limit, art. 12 states that an enterprise's annual environmental information disclosure report according to law shall include the following contents:
(1) Basic information of the enterprise, including basic information on production and ecological environment protection of the enterprise;
(...)
(4) Carbon emission information, including information on emissions, emission facilities, etc.

Article 15 states that "when disclosing annual environmental information, listed companies and bond-issuing enterprises shall disclose relevant information in accordance with the following provisions in addition to the environmental information specified in Article 12:
(1) If a listed company raises funds by issuing stocks, bonds, depositary receipts, medium-term notes, short-term financing bills, ultra-short-term financing bills, asset securitisation, bank loans, etc., it shall disclose the annual financing form, amount, investment direction and other information, as well as information on climate change, ecological and environmental protection of the projects invested by the financing;
(2) Where a bond-issuing enterprise raises funds by issuing stocks, bonds, depositary receipts, exchangeable bonds, medium-term notes, short-term financing bills, ultra-short-term financing bills, asset securitization, bank loans, etc., it shall disclose the annual financing form and amount , investment direction and other information, as well as information on climate change, ecological and environmental protection of the projects invested by financing."
Document Title: Administrative Measures for Legal (ESG) Disclosure of Enterprise Environmental Information

Family Name: 2050 Carbon Neutrality Roadmap for the Marine and Fisheries Sector
Family Summary:
The Roadmap 2050 Carbon Neutrality Roadmap for the Marine and Fisheries Sector setts the sector’s net greenhouse gas emissions target for 2050 at -3.24 million tons. This is a proactive goal that represents a reduction of 7.3 million tons compared with the 2018 emissions of the marine and fisheries sector. The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries set the target with the intention of pursuing a wide variety of policy measures, including replacing fossil fuels with marine energy and maximizing the absorption of blue carbon.

The Roadmap covers the sectors of: Shipping; Fisheries and fishing villages; Marine energy; Blue carbon; Ports; and other sectors and basis for implementation (carbon capture and storage and marine waste).
Document Title: 2050 Carbon Neutrality Roadmap for the Marine and Fisheries Sector

Family Name: Agreement on Investments in a continually greener Denmark
Family Summary:
The government and a political majority signed a political agreement on Investments in a continually greener Denmark on December 4, 2021, as part of the 2022 Finance Act. With the green sub-agreement on the 2022 Finance Act (FL22), a new fund of DKK 2.5 billion is introduced with the aim of achieving additional negative emissions of 0.5 million tons annually from 2025 onwards through CO2 capture. The fund operates with a support period of 8 years, which is intended to ensure that the cheapest biogenic sources are not committed long-term to storage purposes, but can be released for utilisation purposes.

The fund can provide support for negative emissions from CO2 capture and storage from biogenic sources and subsequent storage underground. Biogenic sources refer to CO2 capture during biogas upgrading, biomass-based power and heat production, the biogenic share of CO2 captured at waste incineration plants, as well as carbon capture directly from the atmosphere (DACCS).
Document Title: Agreement on Investments in a continually greener Denmark

Family Name: Forest Act
Family Summary:
The Forest Act establishes the Forestry Commission to manage State forests and protect forests. It also establishes a Mining Timber Permit Board and provides for the conservation of timber resources and the compulsory afforestation of private land, and regulates and controls the trade in forest produce.

One of the guiding principles of the Act is that the role of forests and trees in climate change should be recognised, given their unique ability to contribute to both climate change adaptation and mitigation.
Document Title: Forest Amendment Act, 2021

Family Name: Strategy on Agriculture and Rural Development 2022-2028
Family Summary:
This strategy guides the implementation of the Agriculture and Rural Development Program. It aims to transform agro-rural economies by making them more resilient, inclusive, and sustainable. It specifically seeks to improve the efficiency and sustainability of farm production and natural resource management, to support businesses in rural areas, and to create efficient public services through comprehensive institutional and sector reforms.

To advance Kosovo's commitment to climate change mitigation and adaptation, this strategy identifies challenges and opportunities within the agriculture
sector, including challenges in reducing GHG emissions from enteric fermentation and in producing energy from biomass, as well as investment barriers in implementing the climate change adaptation measure of rehabilitating and modernising the irrigation and drainage system in the country
Document Title: Strategy for Agriculture and Rural Development 2022-2028

Family Name: National Climate Change Adaptation Plan 2021
Family Summary:
Madagascar’s National Climate Change Adaptation Plan 2021 is centred around three strategic areas 1) strengthen the governance and integration of adaptation 2) implement a priority sectoral action programme and 3) financing adaptation to climate change. 

Overall, the adaptation plan includes the following goals:

  • Establishment of a green belt to strengthen the fight against desertification and resilience to climate change
  • Strengthening the adaptation of the agricultural sector and the resilience of rural populations in the far South
  • Strengthening the resilience of rural populations through the development and organisation of export sectors
  • Strengthening the adaptation of the fisheries sector and developing warning systems and associated action plans 
  • Improving access to drinking water in urban and rural areas
  • Strengthening early warning systems to ensure the health sector's resilience in the face of climate change 
  • Accelerating reforestation through the operationalisation of the REDD+ mechanism and the development of ecosystem services
  • Improving the conservation of natural forests and the management of protected areas including the development of climate refuge zones in the interior and on the periphery
  • Protection of coastal infrastructures and economic activities (including tourism) against the rise sea level rise
  • Improving early warning systems for cyclones, as part of a regional effort at the level of the Indian Ocean level
  • Development of resilient rice paddies that emit less methane
  • Optimisation of the resilience of new technologies
Document Title: National Climate Change Adaptation Plan 2021

Family Name: Science and Technology Innovation Plan for the Energy Sector in the 14th Five-Year Plan Period
Family Summary: To achieve the goals of carbon peaking and carbon neutrality, this Plan aims to improve the innovation systems and mechanisms, strengthen innovation capabilities and talent development, bolster fundamental applied research, and accelerate the RD and deployment of advanced, practical technologies. These include technologies for source carbon reduction, process carbon reduction; end-of-pipe carbon sequestration; cleaner and efficient coal utilisation carbon capture, utilisation and storage (CCUS); offshore wind power industry technology and energy storage innovation.
Document Title: Science and Technology Innovation Plan for the Energy Sector in the 14th Five-Year Plan Period

Family Name: EU Soil Strategy for 2030
Family Summary: The EU Soil Strategy aims for healthy, resilient soils across the EU by 2050, making soil protection, sustainable use, and restoration the norm. By 2030, it targets combating desertification, restoring degraded and carbon-rich soils, achieving net greenhouse gas removals in land use, reducing nutrient losses and hazardous pesticide use, and improving water and soil quality. By 2050, the strategy seeks no net land take, minimal soil pollution, climate neutrality, and a fully climate-resilient society, while contributing to biodiversity, circular economy, and human health objectives.
Document Title: EU Soil Strategy for 2030

Family Name: Climate Action Plan
Family Summary:
The Climate Action Plan 2021 provides a roadmap for achieving 51% reduction in overall greenhouse gas emissions by 2030 and reaching net zero emissions by 2050.


The Plan lists actions required to deliver on these climate targets and sets indicative ranges of emissions reductions for each sector of the economy.


The Plan seeks to facilitate a Just Transition and suggests a Just Transition implementation plan for the Midlands Region. It emphasises the necessity of fostering citizen engagement and proposes several measures in this regard. The Plan also emphasises the leading role that the public sector is expected to play in the net zero transition through including a Public Sector Climate Action Mandate.
Document Title: Climate Action Plan 2021

Family Name: Long-Term Vision 2050
Family Summary: Nigeria's Long-Term Vision 2050 serves as a precursor to its subsequent Long-Term Low Emissions Development Strategy (LT-LEDS), and aims towards a low-carbon, climate-resilient high-growth circular economy by 2050, halving greenhouse gas emissions compared to the current levels (at time of writing). It aims to remain gender-responsive, and aim for further emissions reductions to net zero in the long term. The vision draws its guiding principles from the National Climate Change Policy (2021-2030)`: a focus on local action, combined with global thinking; sustainable economic growth with robust adaptation; effective citizenship participation; shared vision of social inclusion and stakeholder responsibility; identification of low-carbon-enabling activities; promotion of environmental quality and ecological equilibrium; transparency accountability and equity; robust ongoing monitoring, evaluation and reporting; international partnership/co-operation; policy co-ordination; and good governance.
Document Title: Long-Term Vision 2050

Family Name: Sustainable Finance Framework
Family Summary:
This Framework supports Turkey's sustainability commitments and outlines how it plans to raise Green and Social Sustainable Financing Instruments, contributing to the domestic and international development of the sustainable financing market. Turkey may issue green, social and sustainability financing instruments under this Framework, funding eligible green and/or social projects that conform to the International Capital Market Association (ICMA) Green Bond Principles and Social Bond Principles, and Loan Market Association (LMA) Green Loan Principles.

One of the eligible sustainable project categories is climate change adaptation, with the following impact reporting metrics:

  • Reduced/avoided water loss (in reservoirs / waterways / natural habitats etc.) (m³);
  • Reduction in number of operating days lost to floods;
  • Reduction in flood damage costs;
  • Increase in agricultural land using more drought resistant crops (hectares);
  • Reduction in land-loss from inundation and/or coastal erosion (km²);
  • Decrease in pressure on natural forests, increase in carbon storage capacity.
Document Title: Sustainable Finance Framework

Family Name: National Development Strategy of the Kyrgyz Republic for 2018-2040
Family Summary:
This strategy sets the government's long-term development vision for the country. It was approved by Decree of the President of the Kyrgyz Republic of October 31, 2018 No. 221. 

Point 3.2 of the strategy focuses on the environment, climate change adaptation and disaster risk reduction. It notably identifies the expansion of green space as a key element in reducing the risks of climate change, land degradation and air pollution. 

Greening efforts are further associated with an enhancement of carbon sequestration capacities alongside economy-wide mitigation measures.
Document Title: National Development Strategy of the Kyrgyz Republic for 2018-2040

Family Name: Jordan’s Policy Framework for Cooperative Approaches under Article 6 and other international carbon markets
Family Summary:
The Policy Framework, issued by the Ministry of Environment, outlines the elements to be followed by Jordan to achieve the international targets of mitigating and adapting strategies by cooperating with other members of the Paris Agreement on Climate Change. The Policy Framework was designed following the issuance of the "Report of the Conference of the Parties serving as the meeting of the Parties to the Paris Agreement on its third session, held in Glasgow from 31 October to 13 November 2021", Article 6.2 of the Guidance, and Rules on Article 6.4.  

The Policy Framework regulates the generation, authorization and transfer of Transferred Mitigation Outcomes (ITMOs), which must ensure transparency and governance and promote sustainable development.

The document currently available for this Framework appears to be in draft form. We are searching for the finalised version of the Framework.
Document Title: Policy Framework

Family Name: Presidential Regulation No. 110 of 2025 on Implementation of Carbon Economic Value Instruments and National Greenhouse Gas Emission Control
Family Summary:
This Presidential Regulation introduces several important changes that reshape Indonesia’s carbon governance framework. It replaces Presidential Regulation No. 98 of 2021 on Carbon Economic Value (the Implementation of Carbon Pricing to Achieve the Nationally Determined Contribution Target and Control over Greenhouse Gas Emissions in the National Development). The key elements are:

  1. The recognition of Voluntary Carbon Market (VCM) activities;
  2. The acknowledgement of established international standards, and abolition of the earlier Mutual Recognition Agreement (MRA) mecahnism;
  3. Carbon projects may choose to obtain certification either from the Indonesian government (Sertifikat Pengurangan Emisi – SPE) or from other recognized certification bodies (non-SPE);
  4. Differentiation between Correpsonding Adjustment (CA) units under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement for carbon units authorised for international transfer, and non-CA units that remain within the boundaries of Indonesia;
  5. A centralised registry (Sistem Registri Unit Karbon; SRUK) for all carbon unit data and transactions; and
  6. Continuity of Implementing Regulations: Although Presidential Regulation No. 98 of 2021 is revoked, its implementing regulations (Regulation 21/2022 on Guidelines for Implementing the Carbon Economic Value) remain in effect insofar as they do not contradict the new regulation.
Document Title: Presidential Regulation No. 110 of 2025 on Implementation of Carbon Economic Value Instruments and National Greenhouse Gas Emission Control

Family Name: Presidential Decree No. 85 on the Ministry of Environment, Urbanisation, and Climate Change
Family Summary: The Ministry previously known as the Ministry of Environment and Urbanisation (MoEU) in Türkiye was officially renamed to the Ministry of Environment, Urbanisation, and Climate Change (MoEUCC) on 29 October 2021, as per Presidential Decree No. 85 published in the Official Gazette No. 31643. 14 This change reflects the Ministry's broader mandate, incorporating climate change into its core responsibilities, indicating a shift in focus towards addressing the impacts of climate change alongside urbanisation and environmental concerns.
Document Title: Presidential Decree No. 85 on the Ministry of Environment, Urbanisation, and Climate Change

Family Name: Presidential Decree establishing the Department of Climate Change (No. 85 of 2021)
Family Summary:
This Decree renames the Ministry of Environment and Urbanisation to the "Ministry of Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change" and establishes the Department of Climate Change to adopt measures relating to climate change and the depletion of the ozone layer, determine policies for green development, conduct negotiations, and ensure coordination with other organisations. It sets out the organisation structure, duties, powers and responsibilities of the Department of Climate Change.

The Coordination Council, composed of various Ministers and Presidents of stakeholder organisations such as business associations, is responsible for determining, monitoring, and evaluating plans, policies, strategies, and actions related to climate change.
Document Title: Presidential Decree establishing the Department of Climate Change (No. 85 of 2021)

Family Name: Action Plan for Carbon Dioxide Peaking before 2030 (‘1+N’)
Family Summary:
This Action Plan aims to enable carbon dioxide peaking by 2030 and ultimately achieve carbon neutrality. It covers the 14th and 15th five-year plan periods. It seeks to strengthen the government's ability to mobilise the nation as a whole and involve the private sector into the decarbonisation efforts. It highlights 1) the promotion of innovation in green and low-carbon science and technology, 2) institutional reform in energy and other relevant fields, 3) the development of incentives and constraint mechanisms, and 4) the need to "avoid excessive side effects" of decarbonisation policies, so as to maintain energy security and economic development as the bottom line. The plan also calls for stimulating international cooperation, notably through 1) global climate governance, 2) green cooperation on business, technology, and finance, and 3) making Belt and Road Initiative green.

The Action Plan further seeks to enhance policy support by developing  a unified and standardised carbon emissions measuring and counting system; improve laws, regulations and standards; optimise economic policies; and establish further market mechanisms. It should be implemented through a strengthening of planning and coordination efforts, ensuring that responsibilities are taken at all levels, and develop a strict oversight and assessment system.

The document lists a series of sectoral policy goals which are as following.

Energy demand and supply:
  • Promote coal substitution as well as transformation and upgrading. The document mandates to "strictly control the scale of supplementary coal power" and of coal consumption growth.
  • Develop wind, solar and hydropower according to local context.
  • Develop nuclear power through a safe and orderly approach 
  • Rationally regulating oil and gas consumption. The plan notably promotes alternatives like advanced liquid biofuels and sustainable aviation fuel, the use of liquid natural gas for peak shaving power stations and as fuel for vehicles and ships.
  • Speed up the development of the new electric power system.
  • Raise capacity for managing energy conservation across the board. It notably seeks to introduce an energy budget management approach, intensify energy conservation reviews regarding fixed-asset investment projects, and conduct comprehensive assessments of projects’ energy use and carbon emissions.

Family Name: Report (White paper) on China's Policies and Actions to Address Climate Change
Family Summary:
This white paper was prepared and published to report on China's progress on responding to climate change, share its practices and experiences, and enhance the understanding of the international community on its policies regarding climate change. It defines the government's long-term conceptual vision as aiming at promoting the construction of an ecological civilisation with high-quality development.


The paper reiterates that China's 14th Five-Year Plan outlines a binding indicator of "reducing carbon dioxide emissions per unit of GDP by 18% compared to 2020". It further states that in as of the end of 2019, China exceeded its 2020 target ahead of schedule and in 2020, China announced a new target: to peak its carbon dioxide emissions by 2030 and strive to achieve carbon neutrality by 2060. By 2030, China's carbon dioxide emissions per unit of GDP will decrease by more than 65% compared to 2005, and the proportion of non fossil fuels in primary energy consumption will reach about 25%. The forest stock will increase by 6 billion cubic meters compared to 2005, and the total installed capacity of wind and solar power will reach over 1.2 billion kilowatts. The proportion of non fossil fuels in primary energy consumption is increased by another five percentage points, and the target for increasing the installed capacity of non fossil fuels is increased. The forest storage volume is increased by another 1.5 billion cubic meters, with a clear goal of achieving carbon neutrality by 2060.


The paper also notes that in 2021 China announced that it would no longer build new overseas coal-fired power projects.
Document Title: Report (White paper) on China's Policies and Actions to Address Climate Change

·       Strengthening climate governance and policy frameworks.

Family Name: Global Warming Countermeasures Plan
Family Summary:
This Plan sets out the direction for Japan's countermeasures, including the integrated improvement of the environment, economy and society; green recovery from Covid-19; changing the awareness, behaviour and cooperation of all actors; and contributing to GHG reductions and decarbonisation technologies. The Plan sets out the plans for reducing various GHGs and carbon sinks, including carbon pricing. The Plan also outlines the roles of the state, local governments, businesses and citizens. The measures are aligned to the Paris Agreement and the overseas deployment of countermeasures is also stated.

The Plan was revised on 18 February 2025, alongside the submission of Japan's second NDC. The revised Plan sets the targets of reduction of greenhouse gases in FY2035 and FY2040 by 60% and 73% respectively from FY2013.

Family Name: Ministerial Resolution No. 185-2021-MINAM. Guide for the operation of the Peru Carbon Footprint tool (Resolución Ministerial Nº185-2021-MINAM. Guía para el funcionamiento de la herramienta Huella de Carbono Perú)
Family Summary: Peru's Ministerial Resolution N°185-2021-MINAM establishes the operational framework for the Peru Carbon Footprint (Huella de Carbono Perú) tool, a voluntary digital platform designed to promote greenhouse gas emissions management amongst public and private organisations. Created under Article 55 of the Climate Change Framework Law regulations, this free tool enables organisations to measure, verify, and reduce their GHG emissions whilst contributing to Peru's Nationally Determined Contributions implementation. The platform operates through a four-level system encompassing emissions measurement, third-party verification by accredited conformity assessment bodies, emissions reduction actions, and complementary measures, all aligned with international standards including ISO 14064-1:2020 and the GHG Protocol Corporate Standard.The tool functions as part of Peru's System for Monitoring Adaptation and Mitigation Measures, serving multiple climate objectives including sensitising organisations to emissions measurement through GHG inventory reporting, fostering emissions reductions that support NDC implementation, improving data quality for the national INFOCARBONO system, and establishing synergies between public and private climate initiatives.

Family Summary:
This Resolution from the Board of Directors of the Central Bank of Brazil provides for the forwarding of information on social, environmental and climate risks. The Resolution establishes that financial institutions in segments S1, S2, S3 and S4 must send the Central Bank of Brazil information on the assessment of the social, environmental and climate risks of their exposures in credit operations and securities, and of their respective debtors. This information includes: I - identification; II - economic sector; III - risk aggravating and mitigating factors; IV - outstanding balance; V - social risk assessment; VI - environmental risk assessment; VII - climate risk assessment; VIII - information on how the exposure fits into the concepts of social nature, environmental nature and climate nature defined in the regulations in force relating to the Social, Environmental and Climate Responsibility Policy (PRSAC); IX - information on the emission, neutralisation and absorption of greenhouse gases; and X - location.

This Resolution relates to National Monetary Council (CMN) Resolution 4945/2021.

Family Name: Qatar National Environment and Climate Change Strategy
Family Summary:
The Qatar National Environment and Climate Change Strategy (QNE) was launched in 2021 in Qatar and outlines practical steps to achieve the environment pillar of the Quatar’s National Vision 2030.

The plan sets out Qatar’s commitment to tackle climate change by diversifying the economy, building capabilities, and optimising the use of natural resources. It establishes national climate targets to enhance climate resilience and identifies a number of environmental priorities:

(a)            greenhouse gas emissions;

(b)            air quality;

(c)            biodiversity;

(d)            water;

(e)            circular economy;

(f)             waste management; and

(g)            land use,

indicating that a governance system has been established to implement the strategy, to reach the specific goals by 2030, including reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 25% by the end of 2030, as well as the establishment of 30 air quality monitoring stations by 2023, and the increase in the number of reserves concerning biodiversity.

The QNE states that plans should be reviewed every 5 years.

The QNE outlines national projects which adopt tangible measures to reduce GHGs, including: (i) the largest carbon capture project in the MENA region; (ii) improving the efficiency of the hydrocarbon toxicity treatment; (iii) the Tarsheed program (National Program for Conservation and Energy Efficiency) which conserves electricity and water consumption, including initiatives by Kahramaa, the national water authority, to reduce the loss of desalinated water and to encourage water recycling and reuse; and iv) the building of the Al Kharsaah solar power station with a capacity of 800 MW.

Family Name: Belgium’s recovery and resilience plan
Family Summary:
To benefit from the support of the Recovery and Resilience Facility set up by the EU in the aftermath of the COVID-19-induced economic crisis, Member States submit their recovery and resilience plans to the European Commission. Each plan sets out the reforms and investments to be implemented by end-2026 and Member States can receive financing up to a previously agreed allocation. Each plan should effectively address challenges identified in the European Semester, particularly the country-specific recommendations of 2019 and 2020 adopted by the Council. It should also advance the green and digital transitions and make Member States’ economies and societies more resilient. The Commission validates the plan after which it effectively enters in force and EU subsidies can start flowing towards the member state.

The European Commission has given a positive assessment to Belgium’s recovery and resilience plan, which will be financed by €5.9 billion in grants. 50% of the plan’s total allocation for reforms and investments supports climate objectives, including:
  • Energy-efficient renovation of residential and public buildings: financing renovation wave across regions to increase the energy efficiency of public buildings, social housing and residential buildings. €1 billion
  • Novel low-carbon energy technologies: financing innovative hydrogen projects and the construction of a multi-functional energy platform in the North Sea to connect 2.1 GW of offshore wind electricity to Belgium. €540 million
  • Sustainable transport: financing of 356 green buses for public transport, promoting the deployment of over 78,000 electric charging stations, improving railway infrastructure and intermodal platforms in ports across the country, creating or refurbishing 1500 km of cycling pathways. €920 million

Family Name: Ministerial Agreement No. MMAE-2021-018. Ecuador Carbon Zero Program
Family Summary:
The Ecuador Carbon Zero Program (Programa Ecuador Carbono Cero) is a comprehensive national initiative aimed at promoting sustainable development compatible with climate goals by addressing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions through quantification, reduction, and compensation measures. Rooted in the constitutional principles of environmental protection, living well (buen vivir -  sumak kawsay), and sustainable economic practices, the program incentivises public, private, and community-led organisations to adopt positive climate practices while enhancing competitiveness. It establishes a structured framework to guide organisations in achieving certifications for carbon reduction and neutrality, including the use of international standards such as ISO 14064 and ISO 14067.
This program emphasises the mitigation of climate change by transitioning to sustainable production and consumption patterns. It promotes the conservation and restoration of ecosystems to sequester carbon, reduce deforestation, and generate environmental, social, and economic co-benefits. Key features include the introduction of the “Green Point” (“Punto Verde”) certification, awarded at three levels: Carbon Footprint Quantification, Carbon Reduction, and Carbon Neutrality. The program also incorporates compensation mechanisms through validated initiatives establishing Emissions Compensation Unities (Unidades de Compensación de Emisiones - UCEs) as a transactional system.
Document Title: Ministerial Agreement No. MMAE-2021-018. Ecuador Carbon Zero Program

Family Name: Ministerial Resolution No. 152-2021-MINAM. Methodological guidelines for the formulation and updating of Regional Climate Change Strategies (Resolución Ministerial Nº152-2021-MINAM. Lineamientos metodológicos para la formulación y la actualización de las Estrategias Regionales de Cambio Climático)
Family Summary: Peru's Ministerial Resolution N° 152-2021-MINAM establishes methodological guidelines for the formulation and updating of Regional Climate Change Strategies (ERCC), positioning them as mandatory instruments that operationalise climate action at the subnational level. These strategies, aligned with Peru's National Climate Change Strategy and Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), must incorporate both adaptation and mitigation measures across five mitigation sectors (energy, industrial processes, agriculture, land use and forestry, and waste) and seven adaptation areas (water, agriculture, forests, health, fisheries and aquaculture, tourism, and transport). The guidelines mandate that regional governments integrate climate measures into their Regional Development Plans, Strategic Institutional Plans, Operational Plans, budget programmes, and investment projects.The resolution outlines a structured five-phase methodology comprising Organisation, Territory Analysis, Planning, Implementation, and Monitoring and Evaluation, emphasising participatory processes that ensure effective engagement with state and non-state actors, particularly indigenous peoples. Regional governments must establish working groups within their Regional Environmental Commissions to lead strategy development, ensuring climate risk analysis, identification of greenhouse gas emission sources, and determination of adaptation and mitigation measures with enabling conditions.
Document Title: Methodological guidelines for the formulation and updating of Regional Climate Change Strategies (Lineamientos metodológicos para la formulación y actualización de Estrategias Regionales de Cambio Climático)

Family Name: Climate Action Plan for Ministry of Agriculture and Food
Family Summary:
The Plan was established following the Ecological Defense Council on November 27, 2020, where the Prime Minister asked four ministries with the largest in terms of greenhouse gas emissions, to establish a climate action plan consistent with France's public policies and commitments.

This plan is structured around six axes:

  • Axis 1: Accelerate the development of agricultural practices that reduce greenhouse gas emissions;
  • Axis 2: Develop the potential for carbon sequestration in soils and forest biomass;
  • Axis 3: Support demand and consumption of food products towards practices with less environmental impact, in conjunction with the National Food and Nutrition Program (PNAN);

Family Summary: Peru's framework for REDD+ (Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and forest Degradation) actions, established through this Ministerial Resolution, operationalises the country's commitments under the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) and the 2018 Climate Change Framework Law (Law No. 30754). The framework identifies eight specific REDD+ actions aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions from the Land Use, Land Use Change and Forestry sector whilst enhancing forest ecosystem resilience, particularly for indigenous peoples and rural communities who depend on these ecosystems.The identified REDD+ actions encompass deforestation-free sustainable family agriculture, sustainable forest management, indigenous-led integrated territorial management (RIA and RIAC), community forest management, forest conservation on indigenous and peasant community lands, titling and governance mechanisms with community monitoring, strengthening of Protected Natural Areas, and landscape-scale forest restoration and reforestation activities. The framework emphasises participatory and transparent climate change management measures, positioning Peru's Ministry of Environment as the national authority responsible for monitoring and evaluating climate change management implementation across all government levels.

Family Name: Supreme Decree No. 023-2021-MINAM. Approves the National Environmental Policy for 2030 (Decreto Supremo Nº 023-2021-MINAM. Aprueba la Política Nacional del Ambiente al 2030)
Family Summary: This supreme decree approves Peru's National Environmental Policy to 2030, establishing a comprehensive framework to address the public problem of "diminishing goods and services provided by ecosystems affecting people's development and environmental sustainability." The policy identifies that approximately 18 million hectares of Peru's ecosystems show degradation, with the Land Use, Land-Use Change and Forestry (LULUCF) sector accounting for 53% of the country's net GHG emissions according to the 2016 National GHG Inventory. The policy establishes eight priority objectives, including Objective 5 (increasing climate change adaptation) targeting a 20% reduction in climate-related damages and losses, and Objective 8 (reducing GHG emissions) aiming for 100% compliance with NDC emission targets. The framework addresses key challenges including deforestation (2.28 million hectares lost between 2001-2018), biodiversity loss, environmental quality deterioration, and increased climate risks. Implementation involves mandatory compliance by all public administration entities, with the Ministry of Environment conducting policy through its Directorate General of Environmental Management Policies and Instruments. The policy integrates ecosystem-based approaches, promotes eco-efficient production processes, strengthens environmental governance with citizen participation, and emphasises the recovery of ecosystem services to ensure sustainable development whilst meeting Peru's international climate commitments.
Document Title: National Environmental Policy to 2030 (Política Nacional del Ambiente al 2030)

The framework addresses key challenges including deforestation (2.28 million hectares lost between 2001-2018), biodiversity loss, environmental quality deterioration, and increased climate risks. Implementation involves mandatory compliance by all public administration entities, with the Ministry of Environment conducting policy through its Directorate General of Environmental Management Policies and Instruments. The policy integrates ecosystem-based approaches, promotes eco-efficient production processes, strengthens environmental governance with citizen participation, and emphasises the recovery of ecosystem services to ensure sustainable development whilst meeting Peru's international climate commitments.

Family Name: National Agrarian Policy 2021 – 2030 (Política Nacional Agraria 2021 – 2030)
Family Summary: Peru’s Supreme Decree adopting the National Agrarian Policy 2021-2030 charts a decade-long programme to lift the “low level of agrarian competitive development” that characterises a sector dominated by small-scale family farming (97 % of producers). Grounded in statistical evidence from CENAGRO and ENAHO, the Policy sets a 36 % improvement target by 2030, to be achieved through three priority objectives, fourteen policy guidelines and twenty-two public services. Central measures include: deepening farmers’ vertical integration into value chains; reducing the proportion of subsistence holdings; and enhancing the sustainable management of soil, water and forest resources. Climate variability and change are recognised as cross-cutting stressors that erode ecosystem services and rural incomes, especially in the Andean and Amazon regions; hence the Policy embeds resource-efficient practices, risk-informed planning and support for technological upgrading, all intended to bolster food security, rural livelihoods and Peru’s progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals.
Document Title: Supreme Decree approving the National Agrarian Policy 2021-2030 (Supreme Decree approving the National Agrarian Policy 2021-2030)

Collection Summary: This Communication from the European Commission to the other European Institutions provides an initial roadmap of key policies and strategies required to achieve the European Union's "new growth strategy", centred on the concept of the European Green Deal. It aims at enhancing the union's climate targets and sets four core goals: 1) climate-neutrality by 2050, 2) protection of human life, animals and plants by cutting pollution, 3) helping companies become world leaders in clean products and technologies, and 4) help ensure a just and inclusive transition. These goals should be reached by developing a circular economy, decarbonising the energy sector, renovate buildings, support the industry to innovate, and green private and public transport systems.
Family Name: EU Forest Strategy for 2030
Family Summary: The main goals of the EU Forest Strategy for 2030 are to improve the quantity and quality of EU forests, enhance their resilience to climate change, and support the communities that depend on them. This strategy is a key part of the European Green Deal and aims to contribute to the EU's biodiversity and climate goals, including reducing greenhouse gas emissions by at least 55% by 2030 and achieving climate neutrality by 2050. It includes measures for strengthening forest protection and restoration, enhancing sustainable forest management, and improving the monitoring and effective decentralised planning on forests in the EU with a view to ensuring resilient forest ecosystems and enabling forests to deliver on their multifunctional role. To further support sustainable forest-based bioeconomy for a climate neutral future, the strategy proposes measures for innovation and promotion of new materials and products to replace fossil-based counterparts as well as for boosting the non-wood forest economy, including ecotourism. The Strategy also focuses on sustainable re- and afforestation and is accompanied by a roadmap for planting at least 3 billion additional trees in the EU by 2030.

Family Summary: Honduras' National Policy on Wetlands and Marine-Coastal Spaces (2019-2029) aims to analyse threats and promote the sustainable management of these environments, and acknowledges their significant threat from climate change. On climate issues it prioritises ongoing monitoring and habitat conservation of systems such as mangroves.

Family Name: National Policy of Land Management (PNOT)
Family Summary:
This policy was prepared in 2019 and approved by a ministerial decree published in July 2021. 

Objective 1.2 of the policy is to promote the occupation and development of the territory in a safe and resilient way that contributes to disaster risk reduction and adaptation to climate change.

Guideline 1.2.c states that management tools and mechanisms in land use planning that reduce disaster risk, increase resilience and consider adaptation to climate change by human settlements and strategic infrastructure must be considered. 

Guideline 1.2.d commands to incorporate the functions of natural systems as tools for mitigating threats and adapting to climate change, in order to reduce the risk of disasters that may affect the lives and health of people, infrastructure, services, or the environment.

Guideline 3.1.d promotes public and private investment in all types of infrastructure, and the generation of knowledge that contributes to the sustainable use of critical natural resources, such as water, renewable energies and soils.

Family Name: Central African Republic National REDD+ Strategy
Family Summary: The Central African Republic's REDD+ strategy aims to guide the long-term conservation, restoration and sustainable economic development of forest ecosystems. REDD+ (Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation) is a voluntary framework for climate change mitigation developed under the UNFCCC, with a focus on the challenges faced by developing countries. The strategy names slash-and-burn land clearance, as well as routine burning of silvopastoral systems, as key drivers of forest carbon loss and reduced ecosystem integrity, and proposes expansion of agroecological practices such as the introduction of tree nurseries to rehabilitate coffee plantations as agroforestry systems. It also proposes investment in improved rainwater harvesting, to improve dry-season yields and reduce the rate of land clearance.
Document Title: Central African Republic National REDD+ Strategy

Family Name: National Climate Change Management Agenda
Family Summary:
The Agenda is an updated version of the National Strategy for Climate Change Management Policy for the period 2021-2050, and was approved in Resolution No XIX-490.

The Agenda sets out targets and objectives for 2030, 2040 and 2050 both regarding climate change mitigation and adaptation. The mitigation policy aims at increasing ambition on greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reduction as well as their removals. The Agenda emphasises the importance of mitigation for the sectors energy, transport, industry, agriculture, waste and forestry.

In Chapter IV, the Agenda sets out detailed mitigation targets for the different time periods and sectors. Notably, in section 23.1, the Agenda sets out "to reduce GHG emissions by 100% compared to 1990 levels by switching to innovative, low-emission, environmentally friendly technologies and the use of RES in all economic sectors, including up to 20 % of removals by natural sinks from the LULUCF sector, and the use of environmentally safe carbon capture and utilisation (CCU) technologies to offset GHG emissions in sectors where technological options for zero GHG emissions will not be available."
Document Title: National Climate Change Management Agenda

Family Name: National Electric System Development Program 2021-2035 (Programa de Desarrollo del Sistema Eléctrico Nacional 2021-2035)
Family Summary: The Programa para el Desarrollo del Sistema Eléctrico Nacional (PRODESEN) 2021-2035 is a key planning instrument for Mexico’s National Electric System (SEN), outlining a fifteen-year strategy for electricity generation, transmission, and distribution, in alignment with the National Development Plan. It integrates various planning tools, such as the Indicative Programme for the Installation and Retirement of Power Plants (PIIRCE) and programmes for the expansion and modernisation of the National Transmission Network (RNT) and General Distribution Networks (RGD). The PRODESEN aims to ensure a reliable electricity supply for over 120 million users across two million square kilometres, while addressing the growing demand, reducing electricity costs, and enhancing system reliability. A core objective is to strengthen the role of the state-owned Federal Electricity Commission (CFE) in generation and transmission, including the reactivation of combined-cycle plants and the modernisation of hydroelectric facilities, to support national energy sovereignty and economic development.In relation to climate change and energy transition, the PRODESEN explicitly incorporates Mexico’s international commitments under frameworks such as the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), the Kyoto Protocol, the Paris Agreement, and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. It emphasises the reduction of GHG emissions, targeting a limit of 139 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent by 2030, as part of Mexico’s Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs). The programme promotes the orderly integration of clean and renewable energy sources into the national energy mix, with a significant focus on distributed generation, particularly solar photovoltaic systems, which are projected to grow substantially by 2035. Additionally, it underscores energy efficiency measures and the expansion of electricity access to rural communities, aligning energy policy with sustainable development goals and environmental protection.

Family Name: A roadmap for capture, transport and storage of CO2
Family Summary:
On 30 June 2021, the Government and a broad range of parliamentary parties agreed on A roadmap for CO2 storage – first part of a CCS strategy. The agreement consists of a number of initiatives enabling storage in the Danish subsoil in both the short and long terms. Specifically, the agreement started the process of preparing for the granting of licenses for CO2 storage in the Danish part of the North Sea, so that storage in depleted oil and gas fields could take place as early as 2025. The agreement also enables the import, export and transport of CO2 across national borders. Furthermore, the agreement has allocated funding of DKK 210 million for studies of all relevant and potential storage possibilities in the Danish subsoil with close involvement of relevant municipalities, citizens, etc.

On 14 December 2021, an agreement on A roadmap for capture, transport and storage of CO2 – Second part of a CCS strategy was reached by the Government and several political parties. The agreement focused on the entire CCS value chain (i.e. capture, transport, storage and use of CO2) and aimed at ensuring that the first CO2 capture plants and stores are in operation in Denmark by 2025.

Family Name: Financial Regulatory Authority Decrees No. 107 and 108
Family Summary:
The Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA), which is in charge of supervising non-bank financial institutions and markets, including the stock exchange, issued two decrees on 5 July 2021 requiring listed companies and non-banking financial institutions (subject to a specific threshold) to make annual disclosures pertaining to environmental, social and governance practices. If the issued capital of the company or its net shareholder equity exceeds EGP 500m, the board of directors will have to make certain climate-related financial disclosures. Decree 107 relates to disclosure rules for companies in non-banking financial services. Decree 108 relates to the disclosure rules for companies that issue securities on the Egyptian Stock Exchange.

The disclosures are not expected to be in the form of narrative reports written by the companies. The FRA prepared two forms for the required disclosures and annexed them to the decrees. Each form includes a set of questions that reflect the standards that are being evaluated. The company is required to answer each question with ‘Yes’ or ‘No’, and to write a clarification or comment on its answer. For example, the company may comment that it is in the process of taking specific procedures to comply with this element and that it is expected to finalise these procedures within a specific period. In some circumstances, the FRA determines the information that is required to be clarified.

The environmental disclosures include questions related to environmental operations and supervision, carbon emissions, used energy sources, use of water and waste management. Social disclosures include questions related to gender diversity, wages, turnover rates of employees, non-discrimination, professional health and safety, children, forced labour, and labour rights. Governance related disclosures include diversity in the board of directors, anti-corruption measures, codes of ethics, and data privacy. As to climate-related financial disclosures, they include elements of governance, strategy, risk managements, metrics and targets. The FRA further requires listed companies, targeted by the two decrees, to submit to the FRA a quarterly report stating the procedures that the company has taken or will take in relation to the required disclosures from 1 January 2022.
Document Title: Decree 108

Family Name: Supreme Decree No. 012-2021-MINAM. Adapts the National Commission on Climate Change (Decreto Supremo Nº 012-2021-MINAM. Adecúa la Comisión Nacional sobre el Cambio Climático)
Family Summary:
The Decree Supreme No. 012-2021-MINAM adapts the National Commission on Climate Change (Comisión Nacional sobre el Cambio Climático) to the legal framework established by Law No. 30754, the Climate Change Framework Law, and its implementing regulations. The instrument formalises the Commission as a permanent, multisectoral body under the technical supervision of the Ministry of Environment, with the primary function of monitoring the implementation of national climate policies and international commitments under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). The Commission is designed as a consultative and oversight mechanism that facilitates coordination between state institutions and civil society actors across all levels of government. Its mandate includes tracking compliance with national climate objectives, evaluating policy effectiveness, and generating technical recommendations for decision-making at both institutional and governmental levels.

The Commission’s composition reflects a structured approach to inclusive governance: it comprises 22 state representatives (designated from key ministries, regional and municipal associations, and intergovernmental bodies) and 22 non-state representatives drawn from diverse civil society groups, including Indigenous organisations (PPICC), Afro-Peruvian networks, environmental NGOs, youth collectives, women’s coalitions, trade unions, academic institutions, professional colleges, and private-sector associations. All members, whether state or non-state, possess equal voting rights, reinforcing principles of participatory legitimacy. The Secretariat Technical is housed within the Ministry of Environment and provides administrative and analytical support, while the Commission may convene specialised technical working groups and seek expert input from affiliated public institutions such as SENAMHI, CONCYTEC, SERFOR, SERNANP, OEFA, and CEPLAN. The body operates under an internal regulation that governs procedural matters, including quorum requirements, voting procedures, and meeting schedules. By institutionalising multi-stakeholder engagement and establishing clear mechanisms for information exchange, reporting, and accountability, the decree aims to strength Peru’s domestic climate governance architecture, ensuring alignment with international obligations, particularly those related to transparency, periodic NDC reporting, and the integration of subnational inputs into national climate planning.

Family Name: Procurement Policy Note 06/21
Family Summary:
In light of the UK government's net zero target, passed into law in 2019, the government has issued a Procurement Policy Note (PPN) on government procurement processes to promote the achievement of the net zero target. The provisions of the PPN apply to all central government departments, their executive agencies and non-departmental public bodies ('in-scope organisations). The PNN state that in-scope organisations should "take action to apply this PPN when procuring good and/or services and/or works with an anticipated contract value above £5million per annum (excluding VAT) which are subject to the Public Contracts Regulation 2015 save where it would not be related and proportionate to the contract". The PPN further states that in-scope organisations should include a requirement for bidding suppliers to provide a Carbon Reduction Plan, confirming the suppliers commitment to achieving net zero by 2050 in the UK, amongst other provisions, as part of the assessment process in the procurement of goods and services.


Organisations that fall within the scope of the PPN guidelines must apply the PPN's provisions to procurement processes from September 30th, 2021 onwards.

Collection Summary: The EU Taxonomy Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2020/852) establishes a framework to classify which economic activities are environmentally sustainable, helping investors, companies, and policymakers channel finance toward activities that support the EU’s climate and environmental goals while ensuring they do no significant harm to other environmental objectives.
Family Name: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/2139 supplementing Regulation (EU) 2020/852 by establishing the technical screening criteria for an economic activity qualifies as contributing to climate change mitigation, adaptation or to cause no significant harm
Family Summary:
This Delegated Regulation supplements Regulation (EU) 2020/852 (the EU Taxonomy Regulation) by setting detailed technical screening criteria for economic activities. It specifies under what conditions an activity can be considered to make a substantial contribution to climate change mitigation or adaptation, and simultaneously ensures that it does no significant harm (DNSH) to the other environmental objectives listed in the Taxonomy Regulation.

The Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/1214 amended this document in order to include specific economic activities in the nuclear-energy and fossil-gas sectors, under strict conditions, into the list of environmentally sustainable activities defined by Regulation (EU) 2020/852. The Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2485 amends Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/2139 by adding additional technical screening criteria under the Regulation (EU) 2020/852 (EU Taxonomy)‑framework, for instance regarding Electricity generation from certain low-carbon fuels.
Document Title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2485

Family Name: Sweden's Recovery Plan
Family Summary:
The first pillar of the national policy is the "Green Transition," which includes investments in sustainable transportation, building energy efficiency, and innovative technologies to minimize GHG emissions, with an emphasis on emission reductions, negative emissions, and adaption measures.

To boost tax collection, the Fund also levies environmental taxes. Reduced taxes on employment and enterprise are meant to be exchanged for lower environmental levies.

Sweden also contains alternative measures to implement the Green Transition in its 2021 budget, with policies meant to support its development until 2030 and 2045. The EU RRF plan includes measures to facilitate the Green Transition. All steps in the recovery plan have been examined to ensure that none of them do major damage to the environment.

Energy-related initiatives in Sweden's recovery and resilience strategy:

- Transition of industrial sector (SEK 2.9 billion)

- Climate change (SEK 5.35 billion)

- Energy efficiency of apartment buildings (SEK 4.05 billion)

- Railway investment (SEK 1.50 billion)

Around 34 billion SEK are available for Sweden's entire financial contribution within RRF. With the aid of substantial claimte-smart technology, Sweden hopes to eliminate all GHG emissions by 2045.

Family Name: England Peat Action Plan
Family Summary:
This document seeks to make the country's peatlands meet their Net Zero contribution, but also contribute to wider environmental goals. It calls for responsible management and enhancement of restoration efforts. According to this action plan, the government will take the following measures:

  • develop an updated and detailed England peat map by 2024,.
  • fund at least 35,000 ha of peatland restoration by 2025, through the Nature for Climate Fund and other sources.
  • By summer 2022, have recommendations for a more sustainable future for  lowland agricultural peatlands, developed by the Lowland Agricultural Peat Task Force. 
  • consult on banning the sale of peat and peat containing products in the amateur sector by the end of this parliament. Publish a full consultation on phasing out the use of peat in horticulture in 2021.
  • continue to protect  peat from fire by both phasing out managed burning and reducing the risk of wildfire.

Family Name: Strategy for Sustainable Food Systems, MeaDRI
Family Summary:
This strategy aims to create jobs, improve livelihoods and encourage balanced diets for the Japanese population. To do so, it aims to create smart food value chains, boost human development, boost research and development, and encourage innovation, notably in rural areas. It also sets specific measures to decarbonise the food sector and make it more resilient.

The document also 1) encourages circular economy with increased use of local resources, 2) aims to contribute to the 2050 goal of carbon neutrality via a reduction in the use of chemical pesticides/fertilisers, , and 3) seeks to disseminate energy saving/precision technologies.

On top of a sectoral carbon neutral target, the strategy sets the following goals by 2050:
- 50% reduction in risk-weighted use of chemical pesticides by dissemination of the Integrated Pest Management and newly-developed alternatives
- 30% reduction in chemical fertilizer use 
- Increase in organic farming to 1Mha
- At least 30% enhancement in productivity of food manufacturers (by 2030)
- Sustainable sourcing for import materials (by2030)
- 90% and more superior varieties and F1 plus trees in forestry seedling
- 100% of artificial seedling rates in aquaculture of Japanese eel, Pacific bluefin tuna, etc.
Document Title: Measures for Achieving Decarbonization and Resilience with Innovation (MeaDRI)

Family Name: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations
Family Summary:
The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) released circular SEBI/HO/CFD/CMD-2/P/CIR/2021/562 to introduce new reporting requirements on ESG parameters called the Business   Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR). The Circular is issued in exercise of the powers conferred under Section 11(1) of the Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992 read with Regulation 101 of the Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements Regulations of 2015.

The BRSR is accompanied with a guidance note to enable the companies to interpret the scope of disclosures. This should enable a better quantification and standardisation of disclosures of ESG parameters to enable comparability. Further to this, the BRSR encourages meaningful engagement with stakeholders, including on social and environmental impacts.

The BRSR seeks disclosures from listed entities on their performance against the principles of the National Guidelines on Responsible Business Conduct. Regular reporting on essential indicators is mandatory while report on leadership indicators is voluntary. Entities already preparing disclosure using international frameworks (GRI,  SASB,  TCFD or Integrated  Reporting) are allowed to cross-reference the disclosures. 

Filing  of BRSR is be  mandatory from the financial year 2022-2023  for the top  1000  listed  companies (by  market capitalisation) and replace the existing BRR. Filing of BRSR is voluntary for the financial year 2021-22.

According to Annex II, entities shall disclose Scope 1 and Scope 2 GHG emissions. They shall classify  risk/opportunity as environment or social and provide its description. Climate change risk can include impact on operations, worker health, demand for products or services etc. Climate change opportunities can include cost savings through resource efficiency, development of new products and services, access to new markets etc. Entities shall also report the total waste generated in its activities, with a break-up as per the categories specified in various Waste Management Rules.
Document Title: Annex II to SEBI Circular on Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting by Listed Entities (BRSR)

Family Name: Croatia’s recovery and resilience plan
Family Summary:
To benefit from the support of the Recovery and Resilience Facility set up by the EU in the aftermath of the COVID-19-induced economic crisis, Member States submit their recovery and resilience plans to the European Commission. Each plan sets out the reforms and investments to be implemented by end-2026 and Member States can receive financing up to a previously agreed allocation. Each plan should effectively address challenges identified in the European Semester, particularly the country-specific recommendations of 2019 and 2020 adopted by the Council. It should also advance the green and digital transitions and make Member States’ economies and societies more resilient. The Commission validates the plan after which it effectively enters in force and EU subsidies can start flowing towards the member state.

The European Commission has given a positive assessment to Croatia’s recovery and resilience plan, which will be financed by €6.3 billion in grants. 40% of the plan’s total allocation for reforms and investments supports climate objectives, including:
  • Energy efficiency and post-earthquake reconstruction of buildings: renovating at least 225,000 square metres of residential buildings and 593,000 square metres of public buildings. €789 million
  • Sustainable mobility: upgrading railway lines, autonomous electric taxis with supporting infrastructure adapted for people with disabilities, installing 1,300 charging stations for electric vehicles, introducing zero- emission vehicles and vessels. €728 million
  • Low-carbon energy transition: modernising energy infrastructure
    to connect 1,500 MW of renewable energy, supporting investments for the production of advanced biofuels and renewable hydrogen, financing innovative carbon capture and storage projects. €658 million
  • Support to businesses for green transition and energy efficiency: supporting businesses with projects aimed at boosting green economy, sustainable tourism, investing in green technologies. €542 million
Document Title: Croatia's recovery and resilience plan

Family Name: National Soil Strategy
Family Summary:
The National Soil Strategy is Australia’s first national policy on soil. It was released in May 2021 and sets out how Australia will value, manage and improve its soil for the next 20 years. Healthy soils are central to delivering resilience to climate change and natural disasters, meeting Australia's emission reduction targets, growing its agriculture industry, and securing human health, food and water security, biodiversity and economic growth.

The strategy’s 3 goals are:

  1. prioritise soil health
  2. empower soil innovation and stewards
  3. strengthen soil knowledge and capability.
Document Title: National Soil Strategy
