Family Name: Present Situation and Future Roadmap of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Sector (White Paper)
Family Summary:
This White Paper is authored by Honourable Barshaman Pun, the Minister of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation of Nepal at the time of publication on 8 May 2018. It outlines the current situation and problems in the field of energy, water resources and irrigation and formulates the future road map for this field according to the available resources, equipment and opportunity. The objectives of the White Paper include fulfilling the energy demand of Nepal by increasing access to renewable and alternative energy, to reduce water-induced disasters, and making weather and flood forecasts more effective.

The future roadmap section sets out that, for water, legal and structural arrangements will be made for the construction and implementation of the Integrated National Water Resources Policy; model action plan, rules and regulation will be prepared in province and local level for irrigation development; and the existing water-induced disaster management policy will be revised. For energy, the Electricity Act and Nepal Electricity Authority Act will be revised; the Renewable Energy Development Act will be formulated; and the Electricity Regulation Commmission will be completed.

The roadmap also sets out future hydropower projects; electricity transmission lines and trade; carbon trading plans; and irrigation construction projects.
Document Title: Present Situation and Future Roadmap of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Sector (White Paper)

Family Name: National REDD+ Strategy 2017-2027 (NEC decision 126/2017)
Family Summary: The strategy is a key part of the country's response to climate change and of the Green Growth Development agenda as per the National Strategy for Responsible and Sustainable Development. The NRS aims to strengthen sustainability of Papua New Guinea's forest while helping to improve land use planning and management to ensure forests and environments are protected. The ultimate aim is to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and reduce the vulnerability of communities to climate change.
Document Title: National REDD+ Strategy 2017-2027 (NEC decision 126/2017)

Family Name: Climate Investment Programme  - Operational Framework for Managing and Accessing Climate Finance in the Kyrgyz Republic
Family Summary:
This document was prepared in cooperation with a range of international finance institutions. It aims to finance a range of climate resilient projects that are aligned with climate-related national policies. The programme identifies the following key actions to enable:

  • Improving the quality of climate services;
  • Improving food security from agriculture, through improved water resources, land management and agricultural practices;
  • Making energy supply infrastructure climate resilient;
  • Making transport infrastructure climate resilient;
  • Making municipal water supply climate resilient;
  • Making buildings climate resilient;
  • Increasing the climate resilience of healthcare;
  • Increasing the climate resilience of mining;
  • Enhancing private sector participation in climate resilience;
  • Enhancing the climate resilience of forestry and biodiversity;
  • Enhancing the climate resilience of emergency situations.
Document Title: Climate Investment Programme  - Operational Framework for Managing and Accessing Climate Finance in the Kyrgyz Republic

Family Name: National Wetlands Policy (PNZH)
Family Summary:
The National Policy on Wetland Management (PNZH) in Niger aims primarily to improve food security and population well-being through the sustainable management and enhancement of wetland resources. The Policy's vision is that by 2030, wetland ecosystems will be conserved, viable, and sustainably managed to provide essential goods and services, ultimately reducing poverty and contributing to global biodiversity conservation.

The PNZH is built upon four priority strategic axes, including Knowledge and Degradation Control and the Rational Use of wetlands. Critically, the Policy's strategic actions include a focus on climate change and disaster risk management (item 8.2). Specifically, the PNZH aims to leverage wetlands' natural function to mitigate the effects of climate change and reduce disaster risks, such as severe flooding and droughts, thereby reinforcing the overall resilience of local populations and ecosystems. Implementation relies on core guiding principles, requiring the participation of all stakeholders in securing sites, developing management plans, and integrating wetland issues into national and local development policies.
Document Title: National Wetlands Policy (PNZH)

Family Name: REDD+ National Strategy
Family Summary:
The objectives include the following:

1. To reduce carbon emission, enhance carbon sequestration and enhance climate resilience through both mitigation and adaptation approaches by minimizing the causes and effects of drivers of deforestation and forest degradation, and intensifying sustainable management of forest resources and across the ecological regions.

2. To ensure fair and equitable sharing of carbon and non-carbon benefits of forests among right holders with effective implementation of safeguard measures.

3. To increase livelihood assets and diversify employment opportunities of forest dependent communities, particularly poor, women, IPs and Dalits.

4. To improve and harmonize policy and legal framework to harness carbon and non-carbon benefits; strengthen institutional capability and improve governance of forest agencies and sector

5. To establish and maintain a robust National Forest Monitoring System with strong monitoring, reporting and verification mechanisms.
Document Title: REDD+ National Strategy

Family Name: Agro-Sylvo-Pastoral Sector Policy (2018-2027)
Family Summary: Burkina Faso's Agro-Sylvo-Pastoral Sector Policy (2018-2027) aims to promote the sustainable development and management of the agricultural sector. It aims to increase productivity while combating land degradation and increasing the resilience of agricultural systems to climate change, emphasising water storage and distribution as a key factor in climate adaptation. Alongside proposing improvements in governance, subsidy access and market efficiency, the policy aims to increase the number of protected forest areas, and put more existing protected areas under management, contributing to land-based climate mitigation efforts.
Document Title: Agro-Sylvo-Pastoral Sector Policy (2018-2027)

Family Name: National REDD+ Strategy of Congo
Family Summary: This strategy seeks to combat the direct and underlying causes of deforestation and forest degradation in the country. It covers the period 2018-2030.
Document Title: National REDD+ Strategy of Congo

Family Name: Marine and Water Authority's climate strategy 2018-2020
Family Summary:
Based on the Marine and Water Authority's mission and vision of living oceans, lakes and watercourses, and the environmental analysis in the appendix, the Authority's objectives are:

- Contribute to reduced greenhouse gas emissions and the energy transition by creating the conditions for sustainable renewable energy.

- Work both nationally and internationally for the restoration and protection of natural environments that can function as natural carbon sinks, such as eelgrass meadows, salt marshes and mangrove forests.

- Intensify internal environmental work to reduce the authority's own climate impact.

The Authority works with climate adaptation in the following ways:

- Promote measures that contribute to climate adaptation by increasing the resilience of ecosystems.

- Integrate climate adaptation into work processes such as action programs, guidelines, environmental assessments and statements.

- Promote climate adaptation in the authority's collaborations, networks and stakeholder dialogues.
Document Title: Marine and Water Authority's climate strategy 2018-2020

Family Name: Water and Environment Strategic Investment Plan 2018-2030
Family Summary: The plan, developed in partnership between the Ministry of Water and Environment (MWE) and a US team at Industrial Economics (IEc), establishes long term investment priorities in the water and environment sectors, aiming to facilitate sustainable socioeconomic development while adapting to climate change and maintaining ecosystems valuable to emissions mitigation. A key focus is physical and human capital investment, such as enhancing water storage, wastewater disposal, community training. It also provides for improved weather stations, for weather information distribution, and significant funding for the rehabilitation of wetlands and forests.
Document Title: Water and Environment Strategic Investment Plan 2018-2030

Family Name: National REDD+ Strategy of Côte d'Ivoire
Family Summary:
This Strategy includes climate change-related measures, including strengthening the resilience of agricultural production systems to climate change through the restoration of forest cover in production areas. Other objectives include reducing poverty by increasing the productivity of village plantations of cocoa, rubber, oil palm, and cashew nuts in order to increase producers' incomes and livelihoods; and improving food security by promoting food crops in conjunction with reforestation and perennial crops.

There will be the creation of a working group on the theme of climate change within the Public-Private Partnership platform
Document Title: National REDD+ Strategy of Côte d'Ivoire

Family Name: Decree No. 2018-191/PRN/ME/DD determining the terms and conditions for implementing Law No. 2004-040 on forestry
Family Summary:
The Decree n. 2018-191/PRN/ME/DD provides the application rules for Niger's Forestry Law (Law 2004-040), structured across seven titles. Title 1 (General Provisions) establishes the administrative framework, defines the national forest domain, and mandates the National Forestry Inventory and National Forestry Plan.

A key climate-related element is found in Article 10 within Title 1, which explicitly requires the National Forestry Inventory to track the stocks of sequestered carbon, directly linking the decree to national climate mitigation efforts.
Document Title: Decree No. 2018-191/PRN/ME/DD

Family Name: National strategy on Community Forestry
Family Summary:
This National Strategy for Community Forestry aims to strengthen the capacity of provincial authorities and ensure that the country’s community forestry laws do in fact include and benefit communities. The plan calls for an “experimental phase” over the next five years to gradually provide access to areas of the roughly 700,000 square kilometres of available forest through community management permits and to test different approaches to community forestry through a number of officially recognised pilot projects.

The implementation of the National Strategy should be ensured on four axes:

1. the establishment of a steering committee (national and provincial);

2. the regular convening of the Roundtable on Community Forestry (at both national and provincial levels) to intensify the dialogue between stakeholders involved;

3. establishing a database of local community forest concessions;

4. ongoing monitoring of these concessions to assess the impact on forest protection, as well as drivers of deforestation and degradation.

In French: Stratégie Nationale pour la Foresterie Communautaire.
Document Title: National strategy on Community Forestry

Family Name: Rwanda's National Forest Policy
Family Summary: The National Forest Policy aims to guide the long-term management, conservation and development of Rwanda's forest resources. It notes the importance of forest carbon sequestration for climate mitigation, and the need to ensure that forests and the resources they provide are also resilient to the effects of climate change. The policy aims to ensure sustainable forestry management at all levels, securing biomass supply for rural communities while preventing ecosystem degradation. It supports additional climate-resilient actions such as agroforestry development, and promotes seeking national and international climate finance to support climate-safe forest usage and recovery.
Document Title: Rwanda's National Forest Policy

Family Name: Maldives’ nationally determined contribution (NDC) implementation plan
Family Summary: Maldvies' NDC Implementation Plan is being developed to monitor and evaluate the implementation of the actions proposed in the NDC to ensure that Maldives meet the commitments to the implementation of the Paris Agreement.
Document Title: Maldives’ nationally determined contribution (NDC) implementation plan

Family Name: National Forest Policy Statement (2018-2028)
Family Summary: The National Forest Policy Statement (2018) promotes and establishes a shared vision for Guyana's forests and their use, covering the period 2018 to 2028. Its four overarching objectives are: to derive economic benefits from the forestry sector; forest conservation; forest social governance; and building capacity for more effective delivery of the above aims. The policy aims to value the country's forests for more than timber, while also promoting the efficiency of the timber sector and better integrating wood into the construction sector as a sustainable low-carbon resource. It notes the key role of Guyanese forests in global and national carbon sequestration, preserving them as a net carbon sink.
Document Title: National Forest Policy Statement (2018)

Family Name: NAMA for a Low Carbon and Climate Resilient Livestock Sector in Honduras
Family Summary: This NAMA (Nationally Appropriate Mitigation Actions) sets out a long-term agenda for the sustainable and climate-resilient management of the livestock sector in Honduras. It promotes rotational silvopastoral systems for land resilience and carbon sequestration, as well as significant capacity building measures to provide farmers with better knowledge and access to financing systems. The NAMA also promotes technological solutions such as nutritional blocks to reduce livestock digestive emissions, and biodigesters to turn animal dung into biogas which displaces wood fuel.
Document Title: NAMA for a Low Carbon and Climate Resilient Livestock Sector in Honduras

Family Name: Decision 84/QD-TTg dated 19 January 2018 of the Prime Minister approving the Urban Green Growth Development Plan to 2030 (“Decision 84”)
Family Summary: Decision 84 sets out objectives of creating and developing urban green growth areas in Vietnam to promote the transformation of the urban economic growth model towards green growth, improve competitiveness, and ensure economic development in urban areas that is rapid, effective, sustainable, contributing to job creation, hunger eradication, poverty reduction, improving people's material and spiritual lives, and enhancing the urban system's ability to respond to climate change, contributing to the national commitment to reduce GHG emissions.
Document Title: Decision 84/QD-TTg

Family Name: Accelerated Growth and Sustainable Development Strategy (SCA2D) 2018-2021
Family Summary:
• Based on the government's vision of "makeing the Comoros an emerging country by 2030, respectful of human rights, gender equality and promoting the rule of law" and the Five-Year Investment Program (PIQ) 2016-2021, the SCA2D , as a national benchmark for the interventions of the State and its partners over the period 2018-2021, has set the following objectives: Strengthen the foundations of a structural transformation of the economy with a view to achieving strong, viable, sustainable, equitable and inclusive economic growth,
  •  Improve the quality of life of the population and guarantee equitable access to basic social services,
  •  Ensure rational exploitation of natural resources, in accordance with the principles of sustainable development, while taking into account climate change,
  •  Strengthen good governance and resilience in the face of political and institutional fragility, and promote the rule of law and social cohesion.


The document calls for more production from renewable energy sources, and protecting its carbon sinks.
Document Title: Accelerated Growth and Sustainable Development Strategy (SCA2D) 2018-2021

Family Name: National Plan for the Restoration of Native Forests (PNRBN)
Family Summary: The PNRBN constitutes a support and guidance instrument for decision-making in national and provincial jurisdictions and forest development processes, within the framework of the National Strategy for mitigation and adaptation to Climate Change. The Plan proposes to develop a program for a first period of six years (2018-2023) in order to reach the goal of 18,000 hectares of native forest restored by 2023. The promotion of ecological restoration, recovery and restoration is defined as a general objective. rehabilitation of the native forest of Argentina with different degrees of degradation in the provision of ecosystem goods and services, which lead to the recovery and conservation of biological diversity and forest biomass, within a framework of mitigation and adaptation policies to environmental changes global current and development established. The following are established as specific objectives: a) restore the functional processes of native forests and their biodiversity; b) identify priority regions; c) promote the necessary alliances for the implementation of the national restoration strategy; d) recover the productive value of the native forest; e) promote the reduction of forest degradation factors, coordinating with Local Authorities; f) promote the reduction and compensation of GHG emissions from deforestation and degradation; g) generate environmental awareness about the importance of the native forest in the different social actors that act on them directly or indirectly; h) link restoration to socio-economic processes established for development, promoting the generation of benefits and ensuring the participation of all actors and sectors of society, cultural and multi-ethnic diversity throughout the implementation of restoration processes; i) and identify and add all existing or potential restoration initiatives in order to enhance the impacts, creating a National Native Forest Restoration Database.
Document Title: Resolution 267/2019 approving the National Plan for the Restoration of Native Forests (PNRBN)

Family Name: Strategic Investment Framework for Environment and Natural Resources Management (CSIGERN)
Family Summary:
The Strategic Investment Framework for Environment and Natural Resources Management (CSIGERN) replaces the National Program of Investment for the Environment and Natural Resources. It is a programmatic framework defining interventions related to the environment and natural resource management. It constitutes the reference document for the Ministry of the Environment and Forestry Resources interventions over the period 2018-2022, and serves as a basis for drawing up sectoral development projects and investment projects.

The framework seeks an inclusion of environmental concerns, including climate change mitigation and adaptation aspects, into sectoral policies, and sets a budget to finance actions in forestry and other environments.
Document Title: Strategic Investment Framework for Environment and Natural Resources Management (CSIGERN)

Family Name: Output-Based Pricing System Regulations (SOR/2019-266)
Family Summary:
This document implement an output-based pricing system for industrial GHG emissions with respect to covered facilities where industrial activities are engaged in. These Regulations set out 1) the manner in which a person responsible for a covered facility must, under Part 2 of the Act, provide a report that sets out the information with respect to the GHG emissions limit and cause the report to be verified; 2) the methods to quantify the GHGs from a covered facility and the production from each specified industrial activity engaged in at the covered facility; 3) the manner of determining the covered facility’s GHG emissions limit based on the facility’s production from each specified industrial activity and the applicable output-based standard; and 4) the manner in which compensation is provided for excess emissions and surplus credits are issued.On 15 March 2025, the Regulations Amending the Output-Based Pricing System Regulations: SOR/2025-108 were issued to ensure that the on-site transportation emissions of covered facilities remain subject to carbon pollution pricing, and, in circumstances where the Minister cancels the designation of a voluntary facility in 2025, to align the compliance period for these facilities to end when the fuel charge rate is set to 0$.

The Proceeds from this system fund the Output-Based Pricing System Proceeds Fund, which has two streams: the Decarbonization Incentive Program (DIP) and the Future Electricity Fund (FEF).
Document Title: Regulations Amending the Output-Based Pricing System Regulations: SOR/2025-108

Family Name: National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan 2018-2030
Family Summary: Vanuatu's National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan 2018-2030 acknowledges climate change as a significant threat to the nation's biodiversity and ecosystem services, and emphasises the importance of ecosystems such as mangroves in climate mitigation via carbon sequestration. It contains measures for monitoring biodiversity changes, and enhancing funding to nature recovery projects which include nature-based solutions expected to feed into carbon credit markets. Organic carbon stock is given as a factor for the prioritisation of habitats for restoration and protection efforts.
Document Title: National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan 2018-2030

Family Name: Emissions Trading Scheme Pilot Project
Family Summary:
In 2012, Mexico enacted the General Law on Climate Change (GCCL), which required the creation of a national registry for greenhouse gases and provided orientation to federal, state and municipal authorities toward the authority to establish a voluntary emissions trading scheme (ETS). (https://carbon-pulse.com/44724/) Mexico will launch a pilot national emissions trading scheme in Aug. 2018 with a three-year pilot phase. The pilot is scheduled to last 36 months, between 1 January 2020 and 31 December 2022. "The pilot will cover the energy and industry sectors. Energy encompasses both electricity generation and fossil-fuel extraction and production. Industry includes, among others, the automotive, cement, chemicals, glass, steel, metallurgical, mining, and petrochemicals subsectors, as well as the pulp and paper subsector. Only direct CO2 emissions will be regulated through the pilot, and participation is limited to entities with annual emissions greater than 100,000tCO2. The system is expected to cover around 300 entities in this phase, corresponding to approximately 45% of national emissions." (ICAP 2019)

New Developments: In 2017, Mexico began a simulation of a voluntary Emissions Trading Scheme (ETS) and the General Climate Change Law makes the scheme mandatory as soon as its three-year pilot phase concludes. The pilot phase—originally planned to start in August 2018—started operation in January 2020. The ETS will not replace the existing carbon tax.
Document Title: Emissions Trading Scheme Pilot Project

Family Name: Growing a Better Australia – A Billion Trees for Jobs and Growth
Family Summary: This programme aims to plant a billion new plantation trees, to boost the Australian economy and drive jobs and growth in rural industries and regional manufacturing.
Document Title: Growing a Better Australia – A Billion Trees for Jobs and Growth

Family Name: National Carbon Emission Trading Market Power Construction Plan (2017)
Family Summary: In December 2017, China issued an emissions trading scheme plan to reduce its greenhouse gas emissions. In its initial phase, the participants in the trading scheme are limited to enterprises or other other entities in the power generation industry with annual emissions of 26,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide or more. The document sets forth a three phase plan for the implementation of the trading scheme: In the first phase, taking approximately one year, the construction of a unified national data reporting system, registration system and trading system should be completed. An administrative management system for the carbon market should also be established. In the second phase, also taking approximately one year, a simulation of the scheme's operation should take place that "comprehensively tests the effectiveness and reliability of the various elements of the market, strengthens mechanisms for early warning and control of market risks, and improves the administrative management and support system for the carbon market". In the third phase, spot marketing trading for quotas between participants in the power generation industry should be carried out. Rather than a cap and trade system, allocations are made on an output-based allowance basis.The trading scheme completed its first full compliance cycle in December 2021.
Document Title: National Carbon Emission Trading Market Power Construction Plan (2017)

Family Name: Government Decision on National Land Use Guidelines (VAT)
Family Summary:
The Government Decision on National Land Use Objectives (or Guidelines) issued 14 December 2017 by Finland's Ministry of the Environment, replaces the 2000/2008 decisions. Under the Land Use and Building Act, it guides regional and municipal land-use planning and state authorities, ensuring nationally significant issues and international commitments are reflected in planning. It responds to climate change, urbanization, demographic change, and biodiversity loss, and explicitly frames land use as key to meeting Finland's Paris Agreement targets.

It sets five thematic objective groups:

  • functional communities and sustainable mobility
  • efficient transport system
  • healthy and safe living environment and climate adaptation
  • Environment and natural resources
  • Renewable energy supply (bioenergy, centralized large-scale wind power)

The National Land Use Objectives (VAT) are currently under review.
Document Title: Government Decision on National Land Use Guidelines (VAT)

Family Name: Regulation No.70/2017 Implementing REDD+ and Sustainable Management of Forests
Family Summary:
The Ministerial Regulation No.70 is a guideline for the implementation of REDD + (Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation, Role of Conservation, Sustainable Management of Forest and Enhancement of Forest Carbon Stocks) for the person in charge of the National, Sub-National REDD + management agency and REDD + implementer.

This Ministerial Regulation aims to achieve REDD + implementation that is in accordance with the requirements of the UNFCCC COP Decree on REDD + and is consistent with national policies, as well as encouraging REDD + implementers to achieve full REDD + implementation, to support the achievement of targets for Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) implementation in the Forestry sector.

The scope of this Ministerial Regulation includes: 1) REDD + locations, approaches and tools; 2) monitoring, evaluation and guidance.

The implementation of REDD + includes the following activities: 1) increasing institutional capacity and human resources; 2)strengthening REDD + policies and tools; 3) research and development.
Document Title: Regulation No.70/2017 Implementing REDD+ and Sustainable Management of Forests

Family Name: Botswana National Climate Change Strategy 2018
Family Summary: The national climate change strategy of 2018 formalises and operationalises what the country set out in its 2016 draft national climate change response policy. It aims to create a sustainable, climate-resilient, and low-carbon society, and lays out priority strategies for strategic sectors and highlights them as either adaptation or mitigation priority response sectors, as well as cross-cutting themes, such as gender and education. The National Climate Change Action Plan serves as an accompanying document (included here), and provides a clear pathway for the implementation and monitoring of the strategy by providing targets and indicators for each strategy.
Document Title: Botswana National Climate Change Action Plan 2018

Family Name: Forest Investment Program for Uganda
Family Summary: The program guides investments into conserving and developing Uganda's forest resources over the long term, aiming to support sustainable socioeconomic development, landscape-level climate resilience and broader benefits in carbon storage for climate mitigation. It encourages watershed-level planning, and expects to result in reduced deforestation/degradation, efficient governance, resilient livelihoods and economic returns, and attract increased investment in ecotourism and high value-added wood products. It emphasises the need to upscale effective existing projects in forest land management, and to work across the value chain, for instance at the demand side, in promoting more efficient biomass cooking.
Document Title: Forest Investment Program for Uganda

Family Name: National Investment Plan to Reduce Deforestation and Forest Degradation (2018-2022)
Family Summary:
The Investment Plan recognises and contributes to achieving the goal of the national REDD+ Strategy, “to contribute to national reductions in greenhouse gas emissions by improving forest and land management, and to ensure equitable sharing of both carbon and non-carbon benefits among stakeholders.” Improved agricultural practices, forest conservation and management, sustainable management and utilisation of forest resources and mining, appropriate energy sources and capacity development will deal with the multi-sectoral challenges of deforestation and forest degradation in Zambia. The implementation of investments in these areas will also put the country on course towards its contributions to the global sustainable development goals (SDGs) to end poverty, protect the planet and ensure that all people enjoy peace and prosperity. It will equally contribute to the implementation of Zambia’s Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) to the implementation of the Paris Agreement.

This Plan sets out activities and implementing institutions to improve climate resilience and mitigation.
Document Title: National Investment Plan to Reduce Deforestation and Forest Degradation (2018-2022)

Family Name: Common Action Framework for Deforestation-Free Cocoa Value Chain (Cocoa and Forests Initiative)
Family Summary:
This Framework sets out the actions for building a deforestation-free cocoa value chain, underlining the crucial role of forests, biodiversity, and conservation in combating climate change, regulating local and regional climate, and providing other essential ecosystem services that support the resilience of the cocoa sector and local livelihoods.

It promotes community-based models for forest protection and restoration, including among other things, the engagement of local communities and producers in awareness campaigns on the status of National Parks and Reserves and Classified Forests and on the critical role played by forests in climate regulation, soil fertility and the water cycle.

The Cocoa and Forests Initiative (ICF) is a joint partnership of the governments of Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana, and 35 companies in the cocoa and chocolate sector representing 85% of the world's cocoa trade, aimed at eliminating deforestation from the cocoa supply chain. The ICF complies with the Preservation, Rehabilitation and Extension Strategy of the Government of Côte d'Ivoire. It is an essential component. The Ministry of Water and Forests (MINEF) coordinates the Initiative in Côte d'Ivoire.
Document Title: Common Action Framework for Deforestation-Free Cocoa Value Chain (Cocoa and Forests Initiative)

Family Name: Regulation No. 46/2017 concerning Environmental Economic Instruments
Family Summary:
In order to implement the provisions of Article 43 paragraph (4) and Article 55 paragraph 14) of Law 32/3009 on the Protection and Management of the Environment, Regulation No. 46/2017 concerning Environmental Economic Instruments sets out a framework for the introduction of both economic incentives and disincentives to protect the environment and reduce pollution greenhouse gas emissions.

The Regulation provides for inter-regional environmental compensation (or remuneration) for activities such as water system protection, the protection of biodiversity, carbon sequestration and storage, and the preservation of natural beauty, amongst other activities. Such compensation may be carried about by the central government to local governments; local governments with regional governments; and governments with any legal person (as defined in the Regulation). This compensation must be used for restoring the environment; conservation purposes; biodiversity enrichment; community capacity building in preserving environmental functions; the development of renewable energy; sustainable economic development; and the development of supporting infrastructure for any of the above mentioned purposes, amongst others.

The regulation further establishes an Environmentally Friendly Label system that may be applied to goods produced within Indonesia as well as those imported from other countries.

Article 31. e) of the Regulation introduces the development of Waste and/or Emission Discharge Permit Trading System as a possible economic instrument to incentivise environmental and climate protection, to be carried out by the central and regional governments. Article 43. 2) stipulates that the development of this trading system will be used to reduce environmental pollution and regulate the allocation of waste discharge and emissions permits in a “fair and proportional manner”. The Regulation goes on to outline the requirements for the Trading System and Article 52. 2) stipulates that the Waster Discharge and/or Emission Trading system must be implemented no later than seven years from the enactment of the Regulation.
Document Title: Regulation No. 46/2017

Family Name: National Climate Change Policy for Grenada, Carriacou and Petite Martinique (2017-2021)
Family Summary:
The policy objectives for 2017 – 2021 are to;
1) Strengthen institutional structure to support coordination, mainstreaming and implementation of climate change adaptation and mitigation action, along with the systematic integration of climate change adaptation into development policies, plans, programmes, projects, budgets and processes.
2) Build climate resilience in the following priority thematic areas: water supply and sewage management; ‘agriculture, agri-business and food security’39; biodiversity and ecosystems; human health and coastal zone management.
3) Facilitate climate smart (low carbon, climate resilient) infrastructure location, planning, design and maintenance, sustainable land management and reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in the electricity, transport, waste and forestry sectors.
4) Integrate disaster risk management and climate change adaptation, and support funding applications for disaster risk management activities.
5) Strengthen institutional arrangements for the collection, storage, analysis, sharing and use of climate, GHG emission and pollutant/chemical data and information to inform evidence-based decision making.
6) Improve citizens’ awareness of the causes, impacts and appropriate responses to climate change, so that they are in a better position to take independent action and support relevant public policies, and state and non-state activities.
7) Access climate technologies for mitigation and adaption along with capacity building. Increase external climate finance support to Grenada’s adaptation and mitigation process.
8) Advocate for international action on climate change through foreign policy.
Document Title: National Climate Change Policy for Grenada, Carriacou and Petite Martinique (2017-2021)

Family Name: Decree No. 9.179/2017 on administrative infractions and penalties to the environment
Family Summary:
The present decree amends Decree No. 6,514, of July 22, 2008, which provides for administrative infractions and penalties to the environment and establishes the federal administrative process for the determination of these infractions, in order to dispose of the conversion of fines.


Article 140 (on the preservation, improvement and recovery of the quality of the environment) stipulates that mitigation or adaptation climate change is one of the objectives, considered as actions, activities and works included in projects under the scope of the decree.

Family Name: Decree 9.172/2017 (National Emissions Registration System - Sirene)
Family Summary:
Establishes the National Emissions Registration System - Sirene, provides for the instruments of the National Policy on Climate Change referred to in item XIII of the caput of art. 6 of Law No. 12,187, of December 29, 2009, and amends Decree No. 7,390, of December 9, 2010, which regulates said Policy.

Related to this, normative instruction 12/2010 stipulates in art 2 that the IBAMA Licensing Board evaluates, in the process of licensing activities capable of emitting greenhouse gases, the measures proposed by the entrepreneur with the objective of mitigating these environmental impacts, in compliance with the commitments assumed by Brazil in the Convention- United Nations Framework on Climate Change. Art 3 states that the Terms of Reference, prepared by IBAMA, to guide the Environmental Impact Studies for the licensing of projects capable of emitting greenhouse gases, include measures to mitigate or compensate for these environmental impacts in line with the National Plan on Climate Change.

Family Name: Clean Growth Strategy
Family Summary:
The Clean Growth Strategy exposes how the Government intends to foster national income while reducing greenhouse gases emissions, and do so at the least possible cost for taxpayers while maximising the social and economic benefits. The Strategy comes in line with the commitment made under the 2008 Climate Change Act that requires the country to reduce its emissions "by at least 80% by 2050". The Strategy acknowledges that efforts to reduce emissions will have to significantly ramp up in order to meet the fourth and fifth carbon budgets (covering the periods 2023-2027 and 2028-2032). Beyond setting up the strategy to 2032, the document explores electrification, hydrogen and emissions removal as three pathways to 2050.
 
 The Strategy firstly highlights the image of leadership and situation of progress that the country has made in the last two decades. It details the economic opportunities brought by the Paris Agreement for its low-carbon industries, notably thanks to its academic strength, expertise in high-value service and financial industries and stable regulatory framework. According to the document, the low carbon sector could grow by around 11% a year on the period 2015-2030, or four times faster than the overall economy, and "could deliver between £60 billion and £170 billion of export sales of goods and services by 2030". The document also mentions the co-benefits of actions to reduce greenhouse gases emissions on local air quality, public health, the economy and the environment. The Strategy also recalls the objective of energy affordability and the fact that leaving the EU represents an opportunity as "domestic binding emissions targets are more ambitious than those set by EU legislation".
 
 A number of more precise objectives are detailed as following: 1) develop green finance capabilities, including by setting up a green finance taskforce and providing up to £20 million to support a new clean technology early stage investment fund,- 2) develop a package of measures to support businesses to improve their energy productivity, by at least 20% by 2030,- 3) improving energy efficiency and aiming at reducing emissions from homes by 19% and energy use by 9%,- 4) rolling out low carbon heating,- 5) accelerate the shift to low carbon transport and reduce emissions by 29% by relying mostly on electric vehicles,- 6) deliver clean, smart, flexible power,- 7)enhance the benefits and value of domestic natural resources,- 8) and lead in the public sector. The government also commits £2.5 billion of investment in transport (33% of the total), power, cross-sector, smart systems, homes, business and industry, land use and waste.
Document Title: Clean Growth Strategy

Family Name: Green Construction through Wood Program
Family Summary:
The Green Construction through Wood (GCWood) program encourages the use of innovative wood-based building technologies in construction projects. This program supports Canada’s commitment to reach 2030 and 2050 emissions reduction targets under the Paris Agreement and advance long-term priorities regarding greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reduction.

GCWood invests in wood construction projects that generate many benefits, including:

  • reduced GHG emissions from renewable and sustainable resources that help decarbonize the built environment
  • accelerated adoption of innovative building technologies and systems
  • updated building codes that allow for taller and larger wood buildings
  • affordable housing and community infrastructure

Since its launch in 2017, the GCWood program has supported 16 demonstration projects aimed at reducing risks and promoting the broader use of wood-based products in construction. As of March 2023, it has funded 4 tall wood buildings, 10 low-rise non-residential buildings, and 2 timber bridge projects. The program also developed the 2021 State of Mass Timber in Canada report and an interactive map to track and analyse mass timber construction progress. These resources help applicants understand Canada’s advancements in the field.

Upon renewal, the program broadened its scope to include support for schematic designs, innovative wood construction systems, and the use of advanced bio-based building materials in both new and existing low GHG emission buildings. It offers non-repayable funding of up to $1.4 million for eligible project costs.

Future funding will prioritise projects in areas such as prefabrication, modular construction, retrofitting, and adaptable or disassemblable design.
Document Title: Green Construction through Wood (GCWood) Program

As of March 2023, it has funded 4 tall wood buildings, 10 low-rise non-residential buildings, and 2 timber bridge projects. The program also developed the 2021 State of Mass Timber in Canada report and an interactive map to track and analyse mass timber construction progress. These resources help applicants understand Canada’s advancements in the field.

Upon renewal, the program broadened its scope to include support for schematic designs, innovative wood construction systems, and the use of advanced bio-based building materials in both new and existing low GHG emission buildings. It offers non-repayable funding of up to $1.4 million for eligible project costs.

Future funding will prioritise projects in areas such as prefabrication, modular construction, retrofitting, and adaptable or disassemblable design.
Document Title: Green Construction through Wood Program - APPLICANT GUIDEBOOK 2023

Family Name: National Agricultural Planning 2017-2030 (Planeación agrícola nacional 2017-2030)
Family Summary: The National Agricultural Planning 2017-2030 was designed to align stakeholders in the agri-food sector towards shared objectives. It focuses on 38 strategic crops, outlining market strategies, optimal production regions based on agroclimatic and logistical factors, and measures to enhance productivity while reducing costs. The policy emphasises climate-smart agriculture and sustainable practices to address stagnating productivity, alongside strategies to mitigate cross-border pests and diseases exacerbated by climate change threatening food security. It also highlights the need for risk-responsive approaches to natural disasters and conflicts, which disproportionately affect food-insecure regions due to climate-agriculture interdependencies. The framework promotes a regionally tailored development model, prioritising agroclimatic suitability, innovation, and infrastructure investment. It encourages public-private collaboration, capacity-building, and resource efficiency to strengthen resilience and market competitiveness.

Family Summary: Mexico's REDD+ strategy aims to guide the long-term conservation, restoration and sustainable economic development of forest ecosystems. Family Name: National Mitigation Plan
Family Summary: The Department of Communications, Climate Action and Environment published the National Mitigation Plan in July 2017. The "whole-of-Government" Plan aims at setting Ireland on a decarbonisation pathway to 2050. The Plan further includes 100 actions for various Ministers and public bodies to implement its strategy. The Government recognises that this document does not constitute a "complete roadmap" to achieve the 2050 decarbonisation objective, but develops a medium to long term action. The document outlines the emissions profiles, policy frameworks and strategies to achieve climate change mitigation at the national level, and in each of the following sectors: 1) electricity generation, 2) the built environment, 3) transport, and 4) agriculture, forestry and land use. It further quantifies costs and emissions reductions potentials.
Document Title: National Mitigation Plan

Family Name: National Action Plan for Climate Change 2017-2022
Family Summary:
Chile adopted the Plan de Acción Nacional de Cambio Climático 2017-2022 (PANCC-II) in 2017, coordinated by the Interministerial Technical Team on Climate Change, Equipo Técnico Interministerial de Cambio Climático.

This strategic policy document includes a target to reduce the intensity of CO2 emissions by at least 30% by 2030, the promotion of non-conventional renewable energies by promoting an energy efficiency law and reforesting 100,000 hectares of mainly native forest. It also defines 4 other pillars of climate action in addition to mitigation. These pillars are: Adaptation, Capacity Building, Development and Transfer of Technologies, and Financing.The plan has 16 specific objectives and 30 lines of action that are embodied in 96 measures, distributed across the four areas of action mentioned above. Adaptation is prioritised in key sectors such as forestry, agriculture, biodiversity, fisheries and aquaculture, health, infrastructure, water resources, energy, cities, and tourism.
Document Title: National Action Plan for Climate Change 2017-2022 (Plan de Acción Nacional de Cambio Climático 2017-2022)

Family Name: The Swedish Climate Policy Framework
Family Summary: In June 2017, Sweden's Riksdag introduced a climate policy framework with a Climate Act for Sweden. This framework sets out implementation of the Paris Agreement in Sweden.By 2045, Sweden is to have zero net emissions of greenhouse gases into the atmosphere. It outlines the government's policy towards mitigating emissions, as well as specific targets for emissions reductions. It contains three pillars for Sweden's climate change policy: (1) the Climate Act, (2) new goals for emissions reductions, and (3) establishing a climate policy council. The Climate Act provides that Sweden's climate policy must be based on its climate goals, requires the government to present a climate report every year in its budget bill and produce a climate policy action plan that describes how it will achieve its climate goals and balance climate policy goals and budget policy goals. The new emissions reductions it sets are: by 2030, Sweden will reduce emissions from domestic transport, excluding domestic aviation, by at least 70% and will reduce emissions from sectors covered by the EU Effort Sharing Regulation by at least 63%; by 2040, Sweden will reduce emissions from sectors covered by the EU Effort Sharing Regulation by at least 75% compared to a 1990 baseline; by 2045, Sweden will achieve carbon neutrality. The Climate Policy Council will support the government by providing an independent assessment of whether the overall policy presented by the government is compatible with its climate goals. The council will also evaluate the likelihood of achieving the government's climate policy goals in various policy areas.
Document Title: Information on the Swedish Climate Policy Framework

Family Name: Forest Legacy Program
Family Summary: This program is a federally funded and state-administered plan to conserve forestland in the United States. In 2024, the Forest Service supported 63 projects that will conserve more than 608,000 acres of private forestlands across the United States, ensuring these places will remain for the communities that rely on them. States, local partners, and tribes have helped to identify forests that provide outstanding benefits to the public. These forests will be conserved through conservation easements and land acquisitions. The Forest Legacy Program was established by Congress in 1990 and is administered by the Forest Service.
Document Title: Forest Legacy Program

Family Name: Tarea Vida plan to face climate change
Family Summary:
The State Plan for confronting climate change, Tarea Vida, was approved in 2017 by the Council of Ministers. Its foresees a programme of progressive investments that will be executed in the short (year 2020), medium (2030), long (2050) and very long (2100) terms. Priority areas have been identified taking into account the preservation of people's lives in the most vulnerable places, food security and tourism development. 

Main goals are : 1) to undertake actions and projects for adaptation to climate change necessary in the 15 areas identified as most vulnerable, 2) to conserve and fully recover the beaches of the Cuban archipelago, 3) to ensure the availability and use of water as part of coping with drought, 4) to direct reforestation towards maximum protection of soils, 5) to rehabilitate the coral reefs as the most affected mangroves, 6) to implement, control and evaluate the adaptation and mitigation measures.

For the vulnerable areas, several measures are established : 1) the ban on building new homes in threatened coastal settlements that are predicted to disappear due to flooding, 2) to reduce population density in low-lying coastal areas, 3) to develop new infratructures adapted to coastal flooding, 4) to adapt agricultural activities to the changes in land use caused by sea level rise and drought, 5) to reduce cultivated areas close to the coasts and diversify crops, 6) to plan the urban reorganization processes of the threatened settlements and infrastructures, 7) to start the process with lower cost measures such as induced natural solutions (beach recovery, reforestation).

The plan also insists on the necessity of an environmental education for a possible sustainable development.
Document Title: Confronting Climate Change in the Republic of Cuba: A Task for Life

Family Name: National Policy for Climate Change
Family Summary:
The National Policy on Climate Change promotes adaptation and mitigation in the country. It contributes to the sustainable development of the country, seeking climate resilience and a low-carbon economy. It sets objectives over the short, medium and long term up to 2050. The document defines the human, material and financial resources needed to ensure the functioning of the National System of Response to Climate Change and Variability. 

It further seeks to 1) establish institutional and inter-sectoral mechanisms, 2) ensure the adequate articulation of institutional actions, 3) include mitigation and adaptation issues in the scope of all public policies, 4) enhance climate-awareness, 5) promote renewable energies, 6) reduce greenhouse gases emissions in the transport and industrial sectors, and 7) improve the carbon sequestration function of national forests.
Document Title: National Policy for Climate Change

Family Name: General Principles of Climate Policy until 2050
Family Summary:
The General Principles of Climate Policy until 2050 (GPCP2050) sets long-term GHG emissions reduction targets and economy-wide and sectoral policy guidelines on climate mitigation and adaptation. The Government shall report to Parliament no less frequently than every four years, starting in 2019, on the integration of climate policy principles in preparing and implementing cross-sectoral and sectoral strategies. The policy guidelines shall be reviewed and, if necessary, updated every four years until 2050.

Estonia's long-term target is to reduce GHG emissions by nearly 80% by 2050 compared to 1990 levels. To move towards this target, the interim targets are a reduction of greenhouse gas emissions by 70% by 2030 and 72% by 2040 compared to 1990 levels.

The sectoral policy guidelines for mitigation cover the energy and industry, transport, agriculture, forestry, and land use sectors.
Document Title: Climate policy fundamentals up to 2050

Family Summary: Vietnam's REDD+ Strategy and Action Plan aims to guide the long-term conservation, restoration and sustainable economic development of forest ecosystems. Family Name: Regulation no. 40464-MINAE for the Implementation of the National REDD + Strategy
Family Summary: This regulation defines the National REDD + Strategy. This Strategy will be part of the Forest and Rural Development Program of the National System of Conservation Areas, which will be an instrument that contributes to the fulfilment of the goals of the National Development Plan, Nationally Determined Contributions and current climate policies (National Climate Change Strategy and Action Plan), as well as the National Forest Development Plan 2011-2020, through actions that help to prevent deforestation and degradation of forests, favouring their conservation and sustainable management, and an increase in carbon stocks. The entire REDD + strategy and the actions that are executed must be framed within the National Climate Change Strategy and the sectoral policies on Climate Change.Art. 4 states that the Strategy must be financed with resources that generate their development through market instruments or non-market approaches, through individuals, companies, or public or private entities, national or international.This regulation repeals Executive Decree no. 37352-MINAE of November 2012.
Document Title: Regulation no. 40464-MINAE for the Implementation of the National REDD + Strategy

Family Name: Climate Protection Policy
Family Summary:
The Climate Protection Policy (CPP) of 2017 is a strategy in the field of climate protection up to 2030 as well as a plan which contributes towards gradual transition to low emission economy up to 2050. It focuses on measures to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and therefore it is a complementary to the 2015 Strategy on Adaptation to Climate Change. The implementation of the CPP will be evaluated by the end of 2021 and updated by the end of 2023. The document 1) addresses the national trends in GHG emissions, 2) sets the objectives and priorities of the country to reduce the emissions, 3) project scenarios up to 2030 and 2050, 4) establishes sectoral mitigation policies and measures, 5) discusses costs and financing of the proposed policies, and 6) addresses the necessary evaluation and reporting procedures. This policy was adopted by Government resolution No. 207 of 22nd March 2017. It updates the 2004 National Programme to Abate the Climate Change Impacts.

It was approved by the Government Resolution 207/2017 and it replacedNational Programme to Abate the Climate Change Impacts in the Czech Republic (OPOK).

Family Name: Long-term Low-carbon vision
Family Summary:
This Long-Term Low-carbon Vision sets out the aim to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 80% by 2050, in light of the Paris Agreement, through energy efficiency, low-carbon energy supply and switch to low-carbon energies in end-use. The policy direction includes full usage of existing technologies, know-how and findings, development and deployment of new innovation, and full mobilisation of all effective policies and measures including carbon pricing. Under this Vision, climate change policy is meant to take a central role for Japan's growth strategy, with Japan aiming to be the forerunner country to provide low-carbon solutions to contribute to global and domestic greenhouse gas reduction.

Climate change policy is meant to also resolve economic and social issues, with the utilisation of local energy resulting in the creation of business and jobs, and the increase in climate and energy security. This Vision outlines the sectors and technologies that Japan is seeking to develop.

This Vision was meant to be a basic principle for long-term significant reduction of green house gases and a preparation document for the formulation and communication of long-term low green house gas emission development strategy. See Japan's Long-term Strategy under the Paris Agreement: https://climate-laws.org/document/the-long-term-strategy-under-the-paris-agreement_7e0b?l=japanq=emission

Family Name: National Climate Change Action Guidelines
Family Summary:
The Environmental Protection Administration of the Executive Yuan passed the first National Climate Change Action Guidelines in February 2017 (in accordance with the 2015 Greenhouse Gas Reduction and Management Act). The Action Guidelines set out the principles and policies for Taiwan's greenhouse gas mitigation and climate change adaptation actions. The policy includes six major sectors for emissions reductions, and eight major areas of climate change adaptation. According to the Act, the Action Guidelines should be reviewed at least once every four years by the central competent authority. 

In 2023, the Action Guidelines were amended to align and respond to Taiwan's Pathway to Net-zero Emissions in 2050. The updated Guidelines incorporate the 2050 net zero emissions target, adds a section on just transition, carbon fee and emissions trading, risk assessment and nature-based solutions.

Family Summary:
The purpose of this decree is the creation of the National Climate Coordination (CN-Climat), which is an organ of the Ministry in charge of the Environment. The main goal of this organ is the "elaboration and strategic orientation of the national policy on climate change". Its responsibilities include:

  • Defining a long-term vision for climate change policy and measures.
  • Coordinating the integration of climate change into national, sectoral, and local development policies, programs, and projects.
  • Coordinating the implementation of the Green Climate Fund.
  • Ensuring compliance with international commitments made by the Central African Republic on climate change

Family Name: Decree No. 8.972/2017 creating the National Policy for the Recovery of Native Vegetation
Family Summary:
This Decree creates the National Policy for the Recovery of Native Vegetation -Proveg. It establishes its objectives and guidelines, and defines its governance. Proveg has within its main objectives to articulate, integrate and promote policies, programmes and actions that encourage the recovery of forests and other forms of native vegetation; and to promote the environmental regulation of Brazilian rural properties, under the terms of Law 12.651 of 25 May 2011.

It's guidelines are: 1) promoting adaptation to climate change and mitigating its effects; 2) prevention of natural disasters; 3) Protection of water resources and soil conservation; 4) encouraging the conservation and restoration of biodiversity and ecosystems services; 5) Provide incentives for the recovery of the Permanent Preservation Areas, Legal Reserve Areas and Areas of Restricted Use; 6) Stimulus of native vegetation.

Family Name: Strategy for Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (ENDE-REDD+) 2018-2030
Family Summary: For the 2018-2030 period, Nicaragua reaffirms its commitment to continue working toward a green development model, focused on care, love, and respect for Mother Earth. This includes promoting the national reforestation campaign in key areas of national interest at a rate of 30,000 hectares per year. Additionally, the country is advancing the National Program to Reduce Deforestation and Forest Degradation (ENDE-REDD), particularly the Program to Combat Poverty and Climate Change in the Caribbean Coast, the Bosawas Biosphere Reserve, and the Indio Maíz Biological Reserve. The goal is to reduce emissions from land-use change by 11 million tons of CO2 equivalent (TCO2e) over five years, along with social and environmental co-benefits such as biodiversity, watersheds, and food security. The country also aims to restore 2.8 million hectares by 2020 under the Bonn Challenge initiative.

Family Name: National Energy Strategy
Family Summary: The National Energy Strategy (NES), which has a double time horizon (2020 and 2050), directs efforts towards substantially improving the competitiveness of the energy system and environmental sustainability. The results expected by 2020 are:1) Wholesale prices of all energy sources will be aligned with average European average price levels, resulting in savings of about EUR9bn (USD11.3bn)/year in the overall power and gas bill (from current EUR70bn (USD87.8bn) - assuming same commodity prices).2) Expenditure on energy imports will be reduced by about EUR14bn (USD17.6bn)/year from the present EUR62bn (USD77.8bn), and dependency on foreign supplies from 84% to 67%, thanks to energy efficiency, increased production from renewables, lower electricity imports and increased production from national resources. 3) Private investment of EUR180bn (USD213bn) will be supported by incentives between now and 2020 in renewables and energy efficiency and in traditional sectors (electricity and gas networks, re-gasification plants, storage, hydrocarbon development).4) GHG emissions will fall by about 21% compared to the 2005 level, exceeding the European 20-20-20 targets for Italy.5) Renewable energy sources will account for 19-20% of gross final consumption (compared with about 10% in 2010). This is equivalent to 22-23% of primary energy consumption, while fossil fuel use will fall from 86% to 76%. Renewables will become the primary source in the electricity sector together with gas, accounting for 34-38% of consumption (compared with 23% in 2010).6) Primary consumption will fall by about 24% by 2020 compared with the reference scenario (an estimated 4% below 2010 levels); this exceeds the European 20-20-20 targets of -20%, thanks mainly to energy efficiency measures. To attain these results, the strategy formulates seven priorities, each with specific supporting measures already set in motion or currently being defined:1) Fostering Energy Efficiency2) Promoting a competitive gas market, integrated with the other European markets and with aligned prices3) Developing renewable in a sustainable way, in order to exceed the European targets (\20-20-20\), while at the same time keeping energy bills competitive4) Developing an efficient electricity market fully integrated with the European market; with gradual integration of renewable power production5) Restructuring the refining industry and the fuel distribution network, to achieve a more sustainable system competitive on the European level6) Sustainably raising national hydrocarbons production, which will bring major economic and employment benefits, while observing the highest international standards in terms of security and environmental protection7) Modernising governance of the energy sector to make decision-making processes more effective and more efficient8) Research and development will play a key role in developing technologies that allow for a more competitive and sustainable energy system The NES lays down long-term indicative objectives for 2050. Among the most important:1) The need to strengthen efforts in energy efficiency. Primary consumption will have to fall in the range of 17-26% by 2050 compared to 2010, by decoupling economic growth from energy consumption. In particular, efforts in building and transport will be critical2) The high penetration of renewable energy, than in any of the scenarios envisaged at the time is expected to reach levels of at least 60% of gross final consumption by 2050, with much higher levels in the electricity sector. In addition to the need of research and development for the reduction of costs, it will be fundamental to rethinking the market and network infrastructure3) A substantial increase in the degree of electrification, which will almost double by 2050, reaching at least 38%, particularly in electricity and transport4) The key role of gas for the energy transition, despite a reduction of its weight both in percentage and in absolute value in the span of the scenario
Document Title: Presentation on Italy's National Energy Strategy 2017

Family Name: Kenya Climate Smart Agriculture Strategy 2017-2026
Family Summary:
The broad objective of the Kenya Climate Smart Agriculture Strategy 2017-2026 (KCSAS) is to adapt to climate change, build the resilience of agricultural systems, and minimize emissions for enhanced food and nutritional security and improved livelihoods. The specific objectives of the KCSAS are to (i) enhance the adaptive capacity and resilience of farmers, pastoralists, and fisher-folk to the adverse impacts of climate change; (ii) develop mechanisms that minimize greenhouse gas emissions from agricultural production systems; (iii) create an enabling regulatory and institutional framework; and (iv) address cross-cutting issues that adversely impact climate smart agriculture.

Four broad strategic areas have been identified for KCSAS: (i) Adaptation and building resilience by addressing vulnerability to changes in rainfall and temperature, extreme weather events, and unsustainable land/water management and utilization; (ii) Mitigation of greenhouse gas emissions from key and minor sources in the agriculture sector; (iii) Establishment of an enabling policy, legal, and institutional framework for effective implementation of climate smart agriculture; and (iv) Minimizing the effects of underlying cross-cutting issues, such as human resource capacity and finance, which would potentially constrain the realization of climate smart agriculture objectives.
Document Title: Kenya Climate Smart Agriculture Strategy 2017-2026

Family Name: National Policy for Climate Change
Family Summary: The National Policy for Climate Change aims to incorporate climate change management into public and private decisions to advance in a climate-resilient and low-carbon development path that reduces the risks of climate change and allows opportunities to be seized. The long-term objective is for the country to be carbon neutral.
Document Title: National Policy for Climate Change

Family Name: Afghanistan National Peace and Development Framework (ANPDF) 2017-2021
Family Summary:
The Afghanistan National Peace and Development Framework (ANPDF) is a five-year strategic plan for achieving self-reliance. The Framework presents a long-term development  for Afghanistan by providing consistent high-level guidance to government and stakeholders. It articulates immediate and long term development priorities, highlights key reforms and outlines priority investments needed to achieve development goals.

It sets the economic, political and security context to ensure the development of agriculture, extractive industries and trade. 

The Framework establishes measures to mitigate the effects of climate change, notably in the energy sector but also by expanding agroforestry and reforestation to support environmental conservation and income generation for farmers. It also creates strategies to mitigate the adverse effects of climate change across the trans-Himalayan region.
Document Title: Afghanistan National Peace and Development Framework (ANPDF) 2017-2021

Family Name: Philippine Development Plan 2017-2022
Family Summary:
In 2016, the Philippines Development Plan 2017-2022 was adopted. It was anchored on the AmBisyonNatin2040 (25-year long-term vision). The plan had three pillars: 1) enhancing the country's social fabric; 2) reducing inequality; 3) increasing potential growth.

The plan was updated by the Philippines Development Plan 2023-2028. Its key goals are to reinvigorate job creation and accelerate poverty reduction. Chapter 15 covers climate action and disaster resilience. The priority is to enhance the adaptive capacity of communities and ecosystems that are most vulnerable to natural hazards and climate change. There are three intended outcomes: (a) increase climate and disaster risk resilience of communities and institutions; (b) enhance ecosystem resilience; and (c) enable the low-carbon economy transition.
Document Title: Philippne Development Plan 2023-2028

Family Name: Philippine Development Plan 2017-2022
Family Summary:
In 2016, the Philippines Development Plan 2017-2022 was adopted. It was anchored on the AmBisyonNatin2040 (25-year long-term vision). The plan had three pillars: 1) enhancing the country's social fabric; 2) reducing inequality; 3) increasing potential growth.

The plan was updated by the Philippines Development Plan 2023-2028. Its key goals are to reinvigorate job creation and accelerate poverty reduction.
